### [1] [RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20628)
*Renbiao Jin,Mingxin Yang,Yutian Chen,Junhao Zhuang,Xin Cai,Mulin Yu,Linning Xu,Wenxian Yu,Danping Zou,Shi Guo,Tianfan Xue*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RealVDeblur combines physics-based blur synthesis with a diffusion-prior deblurring framework, featuring frame-wise VAE encoding, an efficient one-step generator, and a Temporal Window Mask for robust, memory-efficient real-world video restoration and improved 3D reconstruction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world video deblurring is hard due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and limited realistic training data; robust restoration is essential for downstream tasks like mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction.

Method: (1) Build a large-scale, physics-grounded blur synthesis pipeline using scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos to simulate camera-induced and object-motion blur. (2) Employ a video diffusion prior for restoration, with frame-wise encoding by disabling temporal compression in the VAE to handle frame-dependent blur. (3) Distill multi-step diffusion sampling into a one-step generator; use a training-free Temporal Window Mask to stabilize inference for long videos with constant memory.

Result: Experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks show superior perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, along with enhanced robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur.

Conclusion: RealVDeblur offers robust, efficient real-world video deblurring by integrating realistic blur synthesis with diffusion-based restoration, enabling stable, memory-efficient performance and improved downstream 3D tasks.

Abstract: Real-world video deblurring remains challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and the scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream pipelines such as mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction. This work presents \textbf{RealVDeblur}, an efficient generative framework designed to improve in-the-wild robustness under diverse real capture conditions. First, a large-scale, physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline is constructed from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos, providing realistic training data covering both camera-induced and object-motion blur. Second, a video diffusion prior is leveraged for restoration; to better accommodate frame-dependent blur variations, temporal compression in the VAE is disabled and a frame-wise encoding scheme is adopted. For practical deployment on long videos, multi-step diffusion sampling is distilled into an efficient one-step generator, and a training-free Temporal Window Mask stabilizes inference beyond the training horizon with constant memory usage. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, as well as improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur. Project page: https://rbjin.github.io/RealVDeblur

</details>


### [2] [Masked Topology Modeling for Self-Supervised Learning on Parametric CAD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20642)
*Heinrich Jiang,Jennifer Jang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A self-supervised pretraining framework for B-rep CAD using Masked Topology Modeling (MTM) with graph-based edge masking and convexity/curve-type prediction, combined with MoCo-style contrastive learning and BFS-reconstruction, evaluated on ABC and a procedurally generated dataset to achieve strong benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the data scarcity of editable, parametric CAD in boundary representation (B-Rep) by developing data-efficient, self-supervised pretraining tailored to B-rep structures.

Method: Propose Masked Topology Modeling (MTM) that masks a fraction of edges in the face-adjacency graph of a B-Rep and trains a head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from encoder features after message passing. Combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive objective over B-rep-aware augmentations and a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective. Pretrain on the ABC dataset and a new procedurally generated dataset.

Result: Reported strong performance on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating effective pretraining for B-rep CAD tasks using the proposed self-supervised framework.

Conclusion: MTM, when integrated with contrastive learning and region-based masked reconstruction on B-Rep graphs, provides a data-efficient pretraining strategy that leverages the intrinsic topology of B-Reps to improve downstream CAD tasks.

Abstract: Computer aided design (CAD) is ubiquitous: virtually any modern object was designed using editable CAD tools. However, with the shortage of available CAD datasets in its native editable and parametric format, boundary representation (B-Rep), it is ever more important to develop data-efficient methods for this domain.
  We present a new self-supervised pretraining task, Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), that leverages the face-adjacency graph, an induced structure unique to B-reps that the encoder can be asked to reconstruct. MTM masks a fraction of edges and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from the encoder's post-message-passing face features.
  We combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations, a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective, and pretraining on the ABC dataset and our new procedurally generated dataset to show strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

</details>


### [3] [Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20660)
*Anita Hu,Maria Shugrina*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Axolotl3D introduces a multi-modal, occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly uses images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud to enable controllable 3D completion across multi-view and occluded scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art results on Toys4K and OmniObject3D, with strong real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current 3D generative models largely rely on complete visibility and single-view inputs, which limits applicability to multi-view, occluded, or editable scenes. While prior work addresses these challenges individually, there is no unified framework for controllable, cross-modal 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals.

Method: Axolotl3D jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud acts as a geometric anchor for faithful shape completion, while camera parameters enforce consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D space. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data to enable robust cross-modal reasoning.

Result: Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both clean and occluded settings, with strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

Conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under multi-modal conditioning, improving multi-view coherence and occlusion handling, with strong implications for reconstruction and editing in real-world scenarios.

Abstract: Recent 3D generative models produce high-quality geometry from a single image using large-scale priors and diffusion architectures. However, they assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Although prior works address these challenges individually, they lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals. We present Axolotl3D, a multi-modal and occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor promoting faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data, enabling robust cross-modal reasoning. Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, as well as strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

</details>


### [4] [ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20670)
*Yordanka Velikova,Mahdi Saleh,Liming Kuang,Benjamin Busam*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ODeform extends Neural ODEs to continuous 4D deformation dynamics of 3D objects by embedding point clouds and material properties into a latent space and integrating a learned velocity field, enabling real-time continuous deformation without discrete steps and with good generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address limitations of discrete-time or computationally heavy physics-based deformation models, enabling real-time, continuous deformation modeling that generalizes to unseen shapes and parameter configurations.

Method: Encode 3D point clouds and physical properties into a latent representation; model dynamics with a neural ODE dz/dt = f(z, t; θ) governing deformation flow in latent space; solve over time using an ODE solver to obtain continuous trajectories; evaluate on unseen parameter configurations and real 3D shapes; demonstrate interpolation/extrapolation; release code/data.

Result: Improved motion prediction accuracy over baselines on unseen physical parameters; successful transfer to real captured objects with novel shapes; effective interpolation and extrapolation of learned dynamics; potential real-time applicability due to efficiency of continuous formulation.

Conclusion: Continuous-time ODE-based deformation modeling offers accurate, generalizable, and efficient modeling of deformable objects, enabling real-time manipulation and simulation; future work includes richer physical priors and broader datasets.

Abstract: Modeling continuous object deformation is important for many computer vision and robotics tasks, such as manipulation and simulation. Existing approaches rely on learning-based methods or physics simulators to model shape deformations. However, these approaches either use discrete time steps or are too computationally intensive for real-time applications. We present ODeform, a novel extension of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space. Our method transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions (like material properties) into a unified latent space. By solving the resulting ordinary differential equations over time, we model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating the need for discrete time steps while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on unseen physical parameter configurations, showing improved motion prediction accuracy over baseline methods. Our experiments further demonstrate a successful transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes, along with effective interpolation and extrapolation of the learned dynamics. Our code and data will be made publicly available.

</details>


### [5] [Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20691)
*Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy,Dunren Che,Haitham Y. Adarbah,Afzel Noore*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SG-CBM integrates coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to ground concept activations in breast ultrasound, improving diagnostic AUROC and spatial faithfulness.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: In concept bottleneck models (CBMs), concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, yielding unfaithful explanations. A data-centric, spatially grounded approach is needed to ensure anatomically plausible evidence and trustworthy explanations in medical imaging.

Method: Propose SG-CBM with two clinically motivated zones per lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion ROI for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. Train concept maps via a grouped spatial grounding objective, while preserving semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Evaluate with five-fold stratified group cross-validation and a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to assess supervision quality effects.

Result: SG-CBM yields improved diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC, and markedly higher spatial alignment of concept evidence. The stress test quantifies the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness.

Conclusion: Data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation are essential for deployable healthcare AI systems.

Abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models provide interpretable-by-design predictions by mediating diagnosis through human-understandable concepts, but in medical imaging, their trustworthiness is often limited by the quality and granularity of available supervision. In particular, predicted concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, leading to spatially unfaithful explanations. We study a data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) that leverages coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to encourage anatomically plausible concept evidence. For breast ultrasound, we derive two clinically motivated zones from each lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion region of interest for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. We train concept maps using a grouped spatial grounding objective and preserve semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the proposed SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. We also perform a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to quantify the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness. Overall, the results underscore the need for data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation for deployable healthcare AI systems.

</details>


### [6] [DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20692)
*Eric Regina,Richard Arnaud,Samir Hadi Cisneros*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A privacy-preserving pipeline for synthetic lung CT slices using Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with a post-generation Supervisor that filters candidates in learned latent spaces via autoencoder embeddings, DPPs, and Stein Kernel Thinning; achieves a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and FID of 0.3290, showing a strong realism-privacy trade-off but with residual re-identification risk.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Enable realistic synthetic medical CT data while mitigating memorization and membership-inference leaks in GAN-based generation, addressing privacy concerns in medical imaging datalakes and benchmarks.

Method: Propose Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training. Introduce a post-generation Supervisor that filters generated candidates in a learned geometric latent space using autoencoder embeddings. Apply Determinantal Point Processes for diversity and Stein Kernel Thinning for sample selection. Evaluate using Privacy Preservation Score and Fréchet Inception Distance.

Result: Best-performing model achieves Privacy Preservation Score 0.549 and FID 0.3290. Geometric filtering reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, but persistent patient re-identification scores suggest that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity; highlights an important privacy frontier.

Conclusion: The approach advances privacy-aware medical image generation via a multi-stage pipeline that blends OT-based generative modeling with latent-space filtering. While it improves against certain leakage channels, substantial re-identification risk remains, indicating the need for stronger privacy guarantees and additional safeguards to address anatomy-level identity.

Abstract: We present a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge. The approach combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline that filters generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning. Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off, with the best-performing model achieving a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and competitive visual fidelity with an FID of 0.3290. While the proposed geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, highlighting an important frontier for future privacy-preserving medical image generation.

</details>


### [7] [U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20705)
*Elijah Danquah Darko,Min Xian,Terence Soule,Tiankai Yao,Matthew William Anderson*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A novel interaction-free refinement framework (U-CFR) for image segmentation that autonomously self-corrects with uncertainty-guided pseudo-clicks, improving efficiency and boundary accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reduce user effort in interactive image annotation by enabling the model to generate corrective signals itself, accelerating convergence and improving boundary precision.

Method: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR): a boundary-aware uncertainty score combining segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to place internal pseudo-clicks. A dual-head network (segmentation and edge heads) shares a common encoder-decoder backbone. Inference uses cascading refinement steps where pseudo-clicks progressively refine the mask.

Result: Outperforms baseline interactive methods by reducing required user clicks (over 10% on Berkeley) and improving initial mask quality and boundary accuracy across standard benchmarks.

Conclusion: U-CFR demonstrates intelligent, autonomous refinement in interactive segmentation, achieving more efficient annotation with sharper boundaries, especially on challenging datasets.

Abstract: Interactive image segmentation is critical for efficient image annotation; however, existing methods often require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly. We propose Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR), a novel inference-time framework that enables models to autonomously self-correct after each user interaction. U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to guide the placement of internal pseudo-clicks. These self-generated clicks target the most ambiguous boundary regions, providing strong corrective signals without additional manual input. To support this process, we design a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder backbone: a segmentation head ensures region consistency, while an edge head sharpens boundary alignment. In inference, U-CFR launches a cascade of refinement steps, where each stage leverages the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to refine the mask progressively. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed U-CFR improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy. It reduces the required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley and offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

</details>


### [8] [Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20780)
*Inpyo Song,Jangwon Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper argues that open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) evaluation is confounded by definition blindness, introducing three definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ) and a definition-contrastive scoring rule (DeCoS) to isolate definition-dependent behavior; experiments show current baselines rely on target-normal separation and underperform on actual definition following, advocating evaluation as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To ensure OWVAD models truly adapt to user-defined abnormality, not just separate anomalies from normals; current metrics can be gamed by generic separation and miss definition-driven behavior.

Method: Decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination; propose DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ to progressively remove shortcuts; introduce DeCoS by subtracting shared anomaly evidence across definitions; evaluate across UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, MSAD with various baselines including VAD/OWVAD and vision-language models.

Result: Definition-conditioned metrics reveal weak definition-following in strong baselines; DeCoS substantially improves performance (7.3–16.0 AUROC on DC-Disc; 15.5–28.3 on DC-DetΔ)); overall, current evaluation overestimates usefulness without conditioning on the definition.

Conclusion: OWVAD evaluation should measure definition-conditioned anomaly scoring; adopt DC metrics and DeCoS to properly assess models’ ability to adapt to user-defined abnormality.

Abstract: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) is expected to detect events that match a user-specified definition of abnormality. This requirement is stronger than generic anomaly localization: in the same video, changing the definition should change which temporal regions are scored as anomalous. We show that current OWVAD evaluation largely fails to isolate this conditional behavior. Standard VAD metrics and the dynamic-definition protocol can be dominated by target-versus-normal separation, allowing models to obtain strong scores while remaining nearly insensitive to the queried definition. We call this failure mode definition blindness. To explain why it is missed, we decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination, and find that the former receives 7.2-26.8$\times$ more weight across common VAD benchmarks. Motivated by this diagnosis, we introduce three definition-conditioned evaluation metrics, DC-Disc, DC-Det$Δ$, and DC-Sel$Δ$, which progressively remove normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection shortcuts. Experiments on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD reveal that several strong VAD, OWVAD, and general vision language model baselines localize anomalous moments but exhibit weak definition following, often with near-zero definition-response margins. To validate that the failure is actionable, we further introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC points on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 points on DC-Det$Δ$. Overall, our results argue that OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

</details>


### [9] [3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20789)
*Xuening Tian,Dieter Schmalstieg,Shohei Mori*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A hybrid 3D inpainting method for Gaussian Splatting that uses one reference-view inpainting plus 3D PatchMatch to propagate textures, resulting in faster, more consistent results with preserved detail.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Iterative diffusion-based 3D editing is computationally heavy and prone to hallucination drift, causing multi-view inconsistencies and artifacts; a method that enforces 3D-consistent appearance with higher efficiency is desirable.

Method: Perform a single generative inpainting on a key reference view to establish an appearance prior. Then apply a 3D-aware PatchMatch to propagate these textures across all other views via cross-view correspondences, bypassing per-view diffusion.

Result: Competitive inpainting quality relative to diffusion-based multi-view methods, with superior rendering speed and view consistency. High-frequency details are preserved across resolutions, and the reconstruction is mathematically consistent in 3D.

Conclusion: 3D-GIMP offers a fast, 3D-consistent hybrid framework for object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting, reducing reliance on diffusion while maintaining or improving quality and consistency across views.

Abstract: Recent advances in 3D scene editing have leveraged iterative diffusion models to update input views. However, this process is computationally expensive and struggles to produce sharp details. Meanwhile, ``hallucination drift'' frequently introduces multi-view inconsistencies, leading to structural artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints. To address this problem, we present 3D-GIMP (3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets Patch Matching), a novel hybrid paradigm designed for high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of diffusing every view, 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, which serves as an appearance prior. We then introduce a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate these reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, effectively bypassing the stochastic nature of frame-by-frame diffusion. By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP maintains high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions while ensuring a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction. Our experiments demonstrate that 3D-GIMP not only achieves competitive inpainting quality as previous methods using diffusion in multiple views, but also outperforms these methods in rendering speed and view consistency.

</details>


### [10] [Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20790)
*Husanpreet Singh,Robert Tran,Ayushree Kharel,Sudipta Banerjee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Evaluates VR iris quality metrics on unconstrained VR data, mitigates off-axis/illumination artifacts with generative models, and shows unimodal vs multimodal (iris + periocular) recognition with ~11% EER reduction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: VR headsets enable seamless, immersive interaction, but unconstrained acquisition degrades iris recognition; robust quality assessment and fusion strategies are needed.

Method: 1) Assess ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom; 2) apply generative-model-based remedies for off-axis gaze, uneven illumination, and specular reflections; 3) conduct unimodal iris and periocular recognition and score-level fusion; report EER and related metrics; provide reproducibility scripts.

Result: Some ISO metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR data; image adjustments help periocular more than iris; multimodal fusion reduces EER by ~11% relative to iris alone.

Conclusion: Data-specific challenges can be mitigated with generative-model approaches; multimodal fusion yields substantive gains; plans to release evaluation scripts to support reproducibility.

Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) headsets (e.g., Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro) provide a seamless user experience due to their fast, frictionless interaction with the physical world in a simulated environment. User authentication relies on biometric cues such as iris in such headsets. However, traditional iris recognition protocols may not be adequate in cases of unconstrained acquisition, which is typical of VR-based data. In this work, we examine three crucial aspects: (1) evaluating ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset and analyzing their limitations, (2) addressing data-specific challenges such as off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection using generative models, and (3) performing unimodal (iris, periocular) recognition and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular). We observe that some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; whereas, image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition performance. We will release the evaluation scripts upon acceptance for reproducibility.

</details>


### [11] [SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20813)
*Jiun Lee,Jaekwang Kim,Sangmin Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SubSplat proposes Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into finer primitives, restoring density from low-resolution inputs and enabling high-fidelity yet efficient novel-view synthesis by aggregating features across views.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting suffers a trade-off: higher input resolution boosts detail but increases quadratic network computation; lower resolutions stabilize cost but yield insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. There is a need to recover density and detail without prohibitive computation.

Method: Introduce SubSplat framework with SPGR to subdivide Gaussians into finer primitives directly from low-resolution features. Enhance reparameterization quality via feature aggregation to capture high-frequency details across multiple views.

Result: Empirical evaluation on RealEstate10K and ACID shows high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency, indicating the method effectively balances reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost.

Conclusion: SubSplat resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and computational cost in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting, enabling efficient, high-quality novel-view synthesis from lower-resolution inputs.

Abstract: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting enables efficient and generalizable novel-view synthesis. However, high-resolution rendering faces a critical trade-off where increasing input resolution improves detail at the expense of quadratically rising network computational cost. Conversely, maintaining low-resolution inputs stabilizes this cost but results in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. To address this, we propose SubSplat, which introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer(SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density directly from low-resolution features. We further enhance the reparameterization quality through feature aggregation, which effectively captures high-frequency details across multiple views. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency. Our results validate that the proposed framework successfully resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting.

</details>


### [12] [Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20819)
*Thomas Kassiotis,Stefanos Gkikas,Nikolaos Smyrnis,Giorgos Giannakakis*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: StressGAT uses a Graph Attention Network with Differential Action Units and MIL for personalized stress recognition; achieves 88.62% LOSO accuracy on 58 participants; emphasizes interpretability by identifying peak stress intervals and expressivity phenotypes.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses the need to capture non-linear, person-specific facial dynamics for acute stress while delivering interpretability for clinical deployment. Traditional RNN/CNN approaches are limited by sequential bottlenecks, lack of personalized baselines, and limited explainability.

Method: Proposes StressGAT: a graph-based architecture that leverages relational inductive bias to model facial dynamics. Uses Differential Action Units to normalize responses against neutral baselines for personalization. Integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to locate peak stress intervals and reveal expressivity phenotypes. Optimizes for both accuracy and interpretability under a LOSO (Leave-One-Subject-Out) cross-validation protocol on a 58-participant stress-induction cohort.

Result: Achieves 88.62% accuracy in subject-independent LOSO evaluation. The MIL component enables identification of peak stress intervals and distinct expressivity phenotypes, contributing to model interpretability in addition to predictive performance.

Conclusion: StressGAT offers a robust, explainable approach for personalized affective monitoring by combining graph-based relational modeling with subject-specific baselines and MIL-based interpretability, achieving strong accuracy while highlighting clinically relevant stress intervals and expressivity patterns.

Abstract: Stress is a dynamic process characterized by significant individual variability in facial expression. Traditional architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often overlook person-specific baselines or lack the representational capacity to model the non-linear temporal progression of distress due to sequential bottlenecks and rigid grid-based constraints. Furthermore, many deep learning models lack the interpretability required for clinical deployment. This study introduces StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages the relational inductive bias of graph modeling to capture complex facial dynamics that indicate acute stress. By using Differential Action Units, the framework normalizes individual responses relative to neutral baselines to achieve personalized recognition. The proposed model achieves 88.62\% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort (58 participants) using a subject-independent, Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation protocol. Beyond predictive accuracy, the architecture integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal distinct expressivity phenotypes. By simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability, this framework provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring.

</details>


### [13] [Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20866)
*Zhijing Yang,Haocheng Lin,Zhihua Xu,Haojie Li,Keze Wang,Liang Lin,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A multi-agent, constraint-verified approach for interior layout generation that enforces structural validity at each step, using Generator-Evaluator-Refiner roles and a Progressive Consensus Mechanism, plus a new InStruct benchmark with 18k+ annotated samples. It outperforms state-of-the-art on structure adherence and design coherence.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the lack of intermediate geometric constraint verification in one-shot diffusion/LLM-based layout methods, which leads to collisions and infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints.

Method: Decompose layout generation into proposal (Generator), verification (Evaluator), and adjustment (Refiner) stages. Use a Progressive Consensus Mechanism to enforce stepwise geometric validation before each placement. Introduce InStruct, a dataset of 18k+ parametrically annotated samples and structure-centric metrics to standardize evaluation.

Result: Extensive quantitative, qualitative, and user-study evaluations show significant improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence compared with state-of-the-art methods.

Conclusion: Agentic Designer advances structure-aware interior layout generation by integrating modular, constraint-verified decision-making and a domain-specific benchmark, enabling more feasible and coherent designs under complex architectural constraints.

Abstract: Generating realistic interior furniture layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints (e.g., walls, doors, and windows) remains a fundamental challenge in automated spatial design. Existing approaches, primarily based on one-shot generation using diffusion models or Large Language Models (LLMs), lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, often resulting in structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints. To address these challenges, we propose Agentic Designer, a progressive, multi-agent framework that formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative and constraint-verified decision process. By decomposing layout synthesis into modular stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, the framework coordinates three specialized agents, a Generator, an Evaluator, and a Refiner, through a Progressive Consensus Mechanism. This mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, thereby preventing error accumulation. To facilitate this structure-aware paradigm and standardize evaluation, we establish InStruct, a comprehensive benchmark that integrates a dataset comprising over 18,000 high-quality, parametrically annotated samples with a novel suite of structure-centric metrics. Extensive quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies show that Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

</details>


### [14] [ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20868)
*Han Li,Si Liu,Zehao Huang,Dongxin Lyu,Longfei Xu,Jiahui Fu,Daxin Tian,Yuliang Xiu,Naiyan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes ViSTR-Bench, a qualitative visual spatial-temporal reasoning benchmark for MLLMs, focusing on dynamic scenes with 15 subtasks and 1,340 video QA pairs; shows current models struggle with spatio-temporal reasoning and lag behind humans.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a need to evaluate qualitative temporal reasoning in dynamic scenes, beyond static images or exact quantitative predictions, to bridge the gap between machine understanding and human-like perception.

Method: Benchmark design guided by temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation; four dimensions (Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, Physical Dynamics); 15 subtasks; 1,340 video question-answer pairs; diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios; evaluates a range of MLLMs.

Result: Empirical evaluation indicates that while state-of-the-art models have strong general video understanding, they exhibit substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and perform far below human levels.

Conclusion: ViSTR-Bench provides a rigorous evaluation framework that exposes remaining gaps in visually grounded spatio-temporal reasoning and guides future research toward improving qualitative temporal reasoning in multimodal large language models.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse expert-level tasks, but they still struggle with fundamental abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous observation of the real world, such as spatial perception and dynamic reasoning. Recent studies have recognized this gap and introduced dedicated benchmarks to evaluate the spatial-temporal capabilities of MLLMs. However, existing benchmarks mostly focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues largely underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Visual Spatial-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark (ViSTR-Bench), a novel evaluation suite designed to systematically assess whether MLLMs can perform qualitative reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes. Guided by the principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation, ViSTR-Bench establishes a comprehensive four-dimensional evaluations covering Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics. The benchmark comprises 15 distinct subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video question-answer pairs spanning diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios. Extensive evaluations of a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs reveal that, despite their strong general video understanding capabilities, current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

</details>


### [15] [Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20874)
*Zhihua Xu,Zhijing Yang,Yufeng Yang,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes WS-MLR benchmark (Web-COCO/Web-Pascal) for webly supervised multi-label recognition and a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework that leverages instance- and category-level representations to identify and correct noisy labels, achieving state-of-the-art results on the benchmark.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses lack of unified benchmarks and fair baselines in webly supervised multi-label recognition and the challenge of noisy labels when using freely sourced web images.

Method: Constructs WS-MLR benchmark with ~300k images for 80/20 categories aligning with MS-COCO/Pascal VOC. Re-implements representative baselines under a unified setting. Proposes DBMLCL: a dual-branch contrastive learning framework that jointly learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations and measures their similarities to detect and correct label noise.

Result: Extensive experiments on WS-MLR show DBMLCL outperforms representative baselines.

Conclusion: The WS-MLR benchmark enables fair evaluation of webly supervised multi-label methods, and DBMLCL effectively handles label noise, yielding improved recognition performance.

Abstract: Training deep learning models with freely available web images can reduce their dependence on costly manual annotations. Although webly supervised learning has been widely studied for single-label recognition, its multi-label counterpart remains underexplored, partly due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols. To address this gap, we construct a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR), including Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting. The two datasets cover the same 80 and 20 categories as MS-COCO and Pascal VOC, respectively, and contain about 300 thousand images retrieved from the Internet using category-word combinations as search keywords. We further propose a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework, which learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations together with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels. Extensive experiments on the benchmark demonstrate that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines.

</details>


### [16] [WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20883)
*Ming Hu,Mingyu Dou,Jianfu Yin,Miaomiao Zhang,Cong Hu,Yao Wang,Bingliang Hu,Quan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: WhereEdit enables localized adaptive editing for one-step text-to-image transformations by identifying semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applying region-aware modulation, achieving superior editing quality while preserving structure and efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing one-step T2I editing methods rely on global semantic changes with limited spatial control, leading to weak, unstable local edits and poor preservation of non-target regions.

Method: WhereEdit identifies target regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to drive edits within those regions while maintaining non-target areas and structural consistency.

Result: PIE-Bench experiments show WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step editing methods in editing quality without sacrificing generation efficiency; region-level supervision further confirms the value of explicit spatial reasoning.

Conclusion: Spatially controlled one-step editing is achievable by region-aware feature identification and adaptive modulation; explicit spatial reasoning improves editing quality and stability in one-step T2I editing.

Abstract: Recent one-step text-to-image (T2I) models enable efficient image synthesis and provide new opportunities for real-time image editing. However, existing one-step editing methods primarily rely on text conditioning for semantic transformation, lacking explicit spatial control over \textit{where} to edit. More importantly, even when spatial constraints are introduced, these methods often struggle to achieve strong and stable semantic modifications within the target regions. In this work, we revisit one-step image editing from a spatially controlled perspective and identify two key challenges: discovering editable regions and achieving effective localized semantic transformation. We reveal that existing methods perform global semantic transport, which limits high-intensity local editing under the one-step setting. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{WhereEdit}, a framework that reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing. WhereEdit automatically identifies semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency. Experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark demonstrate that WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining the efficiency of one-step generation. Additional experiments with region-level supervision further highlight the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step image editing.

</details>


### [17] [Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20889)
*Junhao Chen,Xinghao Chen,Henghaofan Zhang,Zihao Qiao,Saining Zhang,Yongzhi Li,Ruqi Huang,Sisi Li,Yimin Sheng,Jianyi Zhu,Hao Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Lumera proposes a benchmark and pipeline to parse single-image scenes into engine-native, light-aware 3D representations, including object boxes, parametric lights, per-object meshes, and HDR environments; achieves strong box detection and high light recall but has limitations in precise light localization and cross-engine generalization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Editable 3D scenes require inspectable, movable objects and lights that integrate with game engines; current methods struggle with room-scale or baked GI, and lack engine-native representations and parametric lighting.

Method: Assemble Lumera-2K dataset from 2,513 UE5 projects; create Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light by adapting Vision-Language Models to predict object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I). Use per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop to assemble scenes.

Result: Benchmarks show Lumera-Box achieves the strongest aggregated detection/geometry/semantic/layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762) though anchor recall favors WildDet3D; Lumera-Light attains recall 0.998 for non-empty scenes but limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m) with matched lights having median position error 0.261 m, ΔE2000 4.59, Pearson r 0.628.

Conclusion: Parametric lights are a measurable editable-scene target; the work identifies bottlenecks in relational structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization, offering a principled engine-native reconstruction and assembly pipeline.

Abstract: Editable 3D scene creation requires object instances and lights that can be inspected, moved, and imported into standard engines, yet existing single-image methods largely stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation. We introduce Lumera (Light-aware Unified Engine-native Reconstruction and Assembly), a benchmark and reference pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing from a single image. Lumera-2K is built from 2,513 UE5 projects and provides 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views. On this data, Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I), which are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. In a sanitized box benchmark against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D, Lumera-Box obtains the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762), while WildDet3D remains stronger on anchor recall. For lights, Lumera-Light recovers almost all non-empty scenes (recall 0.998) but remains limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, and intensity Pearson r=0.628. These results establish parametric lights as a measurable editable-scene target and expose remaining bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

</details>


### [18] [MAGE-Vein: Multi-Instance Age and Gender Estimation from Finger Vein Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20897)
*Katsuki Tanaka,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki,Masakazu Fujio,Yosuke Kaga,Kanade Oshima,Kenta Takahashi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: MAGE-Vein introduces a multi-instance, multi-task framework for age estimation from finger vein images, using fused data from three fingers and concurrent gender classification to suppress gender-related vascular variation; on balanced data, achieves MAE 6.12 years and r=0.88, challenging prior claims about finger vein limitations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Public finger vein datasets exhibit strong demographic biases and gender-related vascular variation that confound age estimation; previous results may reflect data artifacts rather than modality limits. A robust approach should fuse multi-finger structural aging cues and jointly model gender to mitigate confounds.

Method: A multi-instance, multi-task learning approach (MAGE-Vein) that performs hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers to extract robust aging signs while suppressing imaging noise, with simultaneous optimization of gender classification to remove gender-specific vascular differences.

Result: On a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, the method achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880 between predicted and true ages, suggesting finger vein age estimation is viable when biases are controlled.

Conclusion: The study argues that prior failures of finger vein age estimation were largely due to biased public datasets, and demonstrates that a carefully designed multi-finger, gender-conditioned model can yield reliable age estimates.

Abstract: Age estimation from finger vein images has been widely considered impractical due to severe demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors like gender. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE-Vein, a novel multi-instance, multi-task learning framework. Our approach extracts robust structural aging signs by employing a hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers, effectively suppressing local imaging noise. Furthermore, simultaneous optimization of gender classification conditions the network to effectively eliminate gender-specific vascular variations. Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880. Our results not only overturn the conventional consensus regarding the limitations of the finger vein modality but also demonstrate that previous estimation failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsisaoki/MAGE-Vein.

</details>


### [19] [DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20900)
*Pierre Gallin-Martel,Mika Feng,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DINO-VPT is a lightweight, vision-only framework for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) that uses hierarchical visual prompt tuning with a Prompt Routing Network to inject input-conditioned prompts, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on UniAttackData without multimodal fusion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To build a unified FAS model capable of detecting both physical and digital spoofing threats while avoiding dependence on multimodal fusion and external text encoders, and to do so in a lightweight, efficient manner.

Method: A vision-only architecture that employs hierarchical visual prompt tuning. Prompts are dynamically injected and conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), enabling the model to disentangle diverse spoofing artifacts without multimodal fusion.

Result: On the UniAttackData benchmark, DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods, demonstrating strong generalization and the viability of vision-only approaches for unified FAS.

Conclusion: A properly structured vision-only architecture with prompt-based tuning can achieve state-of-the-art performance in Unified FAS without multimodal supervision, challenging the assumption that multimodal fusion is necessary for robust cross-threat detection.

Abstract: With the increasing diversity of spoofing attacks, there is a growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. While existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate high generalization in this context, they heavily rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. In this paper, we propose DINO-VPT, a lightweight, vision-only framework leveraging hierarchical visual prompt tuning. By dynamically injecting prompts conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), our method effectively disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without requiring multimodal fusion. Evaluations on the UniAttackData benchmark demonstrate that DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. Our results indicate that a properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without the need for multimodal supervision.

</details>


### [20] [Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20903)
*Liu Liu,Freya Huying Tan,Fábio Duarte*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Temporally averaged images (TAIs) can match or exceed full video features for binary engagement classification in urban scenes, while video features excel in dynamic content; TAIs offer a principled, perceptually grounded temporal compression as an alternative to full video encoding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To test whether richer, higher-dimensional visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, by comparing multiple modalities (video features, TAIs, audio embeddings, text descriptions) across continuous and binary judgments, and by examining whether temporal compression can be perceptually sufficient.

Method: Analyze 61 first-person city-walk YouTube videos, segmented into >50,000 ten-second clips. Represent each clip with four modalities: (1) spatiotemporal video features, (2) temporally averaged images (TAIs), (3) audio embeddings, (4) text-based semantic descriptions. Assess human alignment via (a) Spearman correlations for continuous engagement signals, (b) binary high-/low-engagement classification across classifiers and quantiles, and (c) independent two-alternative forced-choice MTurk study comparing TAIs, full video, text, and audio. Perform gap analysis across scene types (activity-driven vs composition-driven).

Result: Video features show strongest alignment along the temporal-richness continuum for continuous measures. For binary high-/low-engagement classification, TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. MTurk results confirm parity: participants identify engaging moments with TAIs as well as full video; text performs worse; audio near chance. Gap analysis reveals dissociation: video features advantage in dynamic, activity-driven scenes; TAIs align better with human judgments in composition-driven scenes with stable spatial structure.

Conclusion: Richer representations are not universally more human-aligned. Perceptually grounded temporal compression via TAIs can rival full-video encoding for perceptual scoring and may serve as a principled alternative in scenarios prioritizing human-aligned judgments, especially for composition-rich content.

Abstract: We examine whether richer visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube segmented into over 50,000 ten-second clips and represented across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Spearman correlation analysis reveals the expected ordering along the temporal-richness continuum, with video features showing the strongest continuous alignment. However, this ordering breaks down under binary classification of high- versus low-engagement moments (the paradigm most commonly used to train perceptual scoring models), where TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. An independent two-alternative forced-choice study on Amazon Mechanical Turk confirms that this parity reflects human judgment: participants identified engaging moments with comparable accuracy from TAIs and full video clips, while text performed substantially worse and audio remained near chance. Gap analysis reveals a functional dissociation: video features are advantaged in activity-driven scenes with dynamic content, whereas TAIs better align with human judgments in composition-driven scenes dominated by stable spatial structure. These findings challenge the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned, and suggest that perceptually grounded temporal compression can be a principled alternative to full video encoding.

</details>


### [21] [FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20922)
*Yingdong Hu,Yisheng He,Yiming Jiang,Zehong Lin,Steven Hoi,Jun Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FA-LAM proposes a focus-aware, multi-view 3D/4D head model with symmetric attention regularization and a dual-phase training regime to disentangle reconstruction and animation, plus a memory-efficient autoregressive 4D reconstruction with visibility-aware token fusion, achieving high-quality animatable Gaussian full heads especially at large viewing angles.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Improve 3D full-head generation quality and animation realism by addressing two key issues in prior SOTA methods: (1) incorrect/noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between reconstruction and animation tasks.

Method: 1) symmetric semantic attention regularization leveraging head symmetry; 2) dual-phase training to separate large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules; 3) autoregressive modification with visibility-aware token fusion for memory-efficient multi-view/streaming 4D reconstruction.

Result: Reconstructs animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, notably in fine facial regions and at large viewing angles.

Conclusion: FA-LAM advances 3D full-head generation and 4D reconstruction by effectively addressing attention and task entanglement, enabling high-quality animatable heads from one-shot input.

Abstract: We propose FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery. The core of our method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches. Our analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation. To address the first issue, we introduce a symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy that leverages the inherent semantics and structural symmetry of human heads. To disentangle the objectives of reconstruction and animation, we develop a novel dual-phase training pipeline that separates the model's capabilities for large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. Moreover, we enhance our model to support multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction in an efficient and memory-friendly manner through a core autoregressive modification with tailored visibility-aware token fusion. Collectively, these innovations enable FA-LAM to reconstruct animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, particularly in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

</details>


### [22] [MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20924)
*Ziyi Wang,Siming Zheng,Yang Yang,Shusong Xu,Hao Zhang,Bo Li,Changqing Zou,Peng-Tao Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A diffusion-transformer framework (MagicMakeup) enabling region-controllable, high-fidelity makeup transfer with identity preservation, using Token-Aligned Region Gating and Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, plus 1024×1024 synthetic/real data pairing for robust evaluation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Overcome three core challenges in makeup transfer: (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment causing spillover and weak regional control, (ii) unclear separation of transfer vs preservation under two-image conditioning leading to attribute–identity coupling, (iii) lack of a high-resolution, identity-consistent, region-labeled dataset for fine-grained supervision.

Method: Propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion-transformer framework with (1) Token-Aligned Region Gating that aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating for precise region editing, (2) Cross-Modal Perception Guidance that aligns text and image features to clarify transfer vs preservation concepts, and (3) a data-generation pipeline producing 1024×1024 region-specific makeup-removal pairs to support unified benchmarking in both synthetic and real settings.

Result: Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate improved regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

Conclusion: MagicMakeup advances region-controllable, high-fidelity makeup transfer by integrating spatial constraints and cross-modal concept disentanglement; provides a unified 1024×1024 benchmark and demonstrates robustness, suggesting broad applicability across diverse makeup styles and identities.

Abstract: Makeup-transfer applies the reference makeup to the source face while preserving the source identity. Despite advances in full-face editing by diffusion-based methods, strong regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation remain challenging. The reasons are (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment that causes spillover into non-target areas and weakens regional control; (ii) unclear transfer/preservation concept separation under two-image conditioning, leading to coupling between makeup attributes and identity; and (iii) the lack of a high-resolution dataset that is identity-consistent and region-labeled for fine-grained supervision. In this paper, we propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable and high-fidelity makeup transfer, built on spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. To enable precise region-specific editing while preserving identity, we propose Token-Aligned Region Gating, which aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating. To clarify the concepts of transfer and preservation, we further introduce Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, which aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception. We also design a pipeline for the generation of 1024 x 1024 data pairs through region-specific makeup removal and establish a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MagicMakeup improves regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

</details>


### [23] [Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20940)
*Zekun Li,Xiaoyan Cong,Hongyu Li,Zhiyang Dou,Chuan Guo,Abhay Mittal,Sizhe An,Srinath Sridhar*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Ms.Forcing presents a streaming video diffusion framework that adapts spatial granularity to per-state noise levels via MSP and MSSA, plus H-DMD to align training with inference, achieving higher throughput with a static computation graph.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address inefficiencies in streaming diffusion for video (nested autoregressive denoising, uniform tokenization) by reducing active tokens and attention cost while maintaining real-time performance and long-horizon stability.

Method: Two core components: (1) Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier frames to cut token counts; (2) Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) scales attention density to the query scale; both yield a fixed, hardware-friendly window schedule. Additional H-DMD approach assembles each generated frame from clean predictions sharing the same source noise to reduce training-inference mismatch. The approach also offsets multi-scale training costs through architectural design and overlapping-window considerations.

Result: Quantitative: 22.84 FPS on an H200 GPU; 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing; improved VBench scores for both short- and long-video generation. Reported 45% reduction in active-window tokens due to MSP.

Conclusion: Ms.Forcing delivers a more efficient streaming video diffusion pipeline with adaptive spatial granularity and stable hardware-compatible computation, complemented by H-DMD to improve training-inference alignment; demonstrates meaningful throughput gains and quality improvements.

Abstract: Streaming video diffusion models have made substantial progress toward interactive and dynamic world simulation, but the nested autoregressive and denoising loops of conventional next-frame generation hinder real-time deployment. Recent rolling-window methods pipeline denoising across multiple consecutive frames at different noise levels, improving throughput and long-horizon stability. However, they tokenize every state at the same fine spatial granularity, leaving substantial noise-dependent redundancy in the joint denoising window. We propose Ms.Forcing, an efficient streaming video generation paradigm that adapts spatial granularity to each state's noise level. Its Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier states, reducing the active-window token count by 45%, while Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches the density of visible non-sink keys and values to each query scale to further reduce attention cost. Because both schedules are fixed by window position, Ms.Forcing retains a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. We further introduce Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD), which assembles each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level, thereby reducing the mismatch between DMD training sequences and inference-time rollouts. The multi-scale design helps offset the additional training cost of backpropagating through overlapping windows. We include both quantitative and qualitative experiments to show that Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, while significantly improving VBench scores in both short video and long video generation setting.

</details>


### [24] [RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20947)
*Junsheng Du,Zhaocheng He,Yuhuan Lu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Region-aware extrinsic compensation (RECO) for robust 3D object detection under camera extrinsic perturbations via piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets, near/far scene partition, differentiable blending, and reprojection supervision.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Camera extrinsics are highly sensitive; small perturbations propagate through projective geometry, causing feature misalignment and localization degradation in BEV-based ITS perception.

Method: Predicts piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets with a learnable range boundary to split the scene into near and far regions; applies region-specific extrinsic corrections; uses a differentiable sigmoid gate to blend compensated geometries; introduces auxiliary reprojection loss comparing 2D projections of 3D GT to 2D annotations, trained jointly with the detection objective.

Result: Demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D under yaw and z-axis extrinsic deviations; generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent calibration shifts and remains competitive under strict calibration uncertainty.

Conclusion: RECO stabilizes BEV sampling by compensating extrinsics in a region-aware, differentiable manner, yielding robust 3D detection under extrinsic perturbations with good cross-dataset generalization.

Abstract: In intelligent transportation systems, roadside 3D object detection provides wide-area perception crucial for traffic understanding, cooperative early warning, and safe autonomous driving. However, existing methods suffer from high sensitivity to camera extrinsics; even slight deviations (whether manifesting as transient jitter or persistent drift) can be significantly amplified by projective geometry. This cascade results in severe feature misalignment and degraded localization. To mitigate this limitation, we propose RECO, a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework that corrects extrinsics using piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets. RECO predicts a learnable range boundary to partition the scene into near and far regions, estimating region-specific pose corrections. A differentiable sigmoid gate then smoothly blends the two compensated geometries to preserve continuous BEV sampling and facilitate stable optimization. To supervise the refinement of extrinsics, we introduce an auxiliary reprojection loss that compares 2D bounding boxes projected from 3D ground truth against 2D annotations, optimizing it jointly with the standard detection objective. Extensive experiments on the DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under extrinsic perturbations demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across both yaw and $z$-axis deviations. RECO also generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent shifts, maintaining highly competitive performance under strict calibration uncertainty.

</details>


### [25] [FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20955)
*Linke Fan,Xianglong Li,Huixin Huang,Kai Shu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FSB-Net introduces boundary-aware segmentation for brain stroke lesions in NCCT by incorporating frequency-domain boundary representations (wavelet features), a bidirectional frequency-spatial attention mechanism, and a spectral boundary loss, built on a PVTv2-B2 encoder; it achieves state-of-the-art Dice, IoU, and HD95 on a public stroke CT dataset compared to U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Accurate NCCT stroke lesion segmentation is hindered by low tissue contrast, heterogeneous lesion morphology across ischemic/hemorrhagic types, and blurred boundaries due to partial volume effects. Existing DL methods optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, limiting boundary delineation for reliable volumetry and planning.

Method: FSB-Net consists of: (i) Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) that applies discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features to extract high-frequency sub-bands as boundary representations; (ii) Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) that enables bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for targeted boundary enhancement; (iii) Spectral Boundary Loss that penalizes high-frequency discrepancies in the Fourier domain to sharpen boundaries. The network is built atop a PVTv2-B2 encoder and evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset.

Result: FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ on all reported metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance in mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95 on the public Brain Stroke CT dataset containing both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases.

Conclusion: The proposed frequency-spatial boundary framework yields sharper, more accurate lesion boundaries and superior segmentation performance for NCCT stroke lesions, suggesting boundary-focused, frequency-domain modeling as a valuable direction for boundary-aware medical image segmentation.

Abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain stroke lesions in non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans is critical for rapid clinical decision-making, yet remains difficult due to the low contrast between lesion and normal brain tissue, heterogeneous lesion morphology across ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes, and ambiguous boundaries caused by partial volume effects. Current deep learning approaches primarily optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, leading to imprecise delineation that can affect volumetric assessment and treatment planning. We propose FSB-Net, a frequency-spatial boundary network that leverages frequency-domain analysis for boundary-aware stroke lesion segmentation. FSB-Net introduces three components: (i) a Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) that applies the discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features, extracting high-frequency sub-bands as boundary representations; (ii) a Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) that performs bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for selective boundary enhancement; and (iii) a Spectral Boundary Loss that penalizes high-frequency discrepancies in the Fourier domain to optimize boundary sharpness. Built on a PVTv2-B2 encoder, FSB-Net is evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset containing both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases. Experimental results show that FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance in mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95.

</details>


### [26] [Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction in Dental CBCT using Fine-tuned Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20977)
*G. L. T. Chamika,S. N. A. Dhanapala,P. H. S. V. Nimalaweera,Maheshi B. Dissanayake,Ruwan D. Jayasinghe*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Unsupervised CycleGAN-based MAR for dental CBCT using unpaired ToothFairy data; U-Net generators and PatchGAN discriminators yield high-fidelity restoration with fast inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address metal artifacts in CBCT dental imaging without voxel-aligned paired data, aiming to preserve anatomy and reduce artifacts while avoiding generative hallucinations.

Method: CycleGAN with U-Net generators and PatchGAN discriminators trained on ~4,000 unpaired ToothFairy images; architecture tuned to minimize hallucinations and preserve morphology; real-time slice-wise inference (~3 ms).

Result: BRISQUE improved by 34.6%, FID reduced from 207.03 to 157.04, SSIM 0.9105; 3.03 ms per-slice inference; expert validation supports fidelity; recommended for clinical decision-support with human-in-the-loop for extreme cases.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a scalable unsupervised MAR solution for dental CBCT with high-fidelity artifact suppression and real-time performance, suitable for integration as decision-support under clinician oversight.

Abstract: Metal artifacts generated by dental implants significantly degrade cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) volumes, obscuring critical anatomical structures and compromising diagnostic precision. To address this, an unsupervised deep learning framework has been proposed for Metal Artifact Reduction (MAR) utilizing a Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) optimized for high-fidelity restoration. Unlike supervised methods that rely on unattainable voxel-aligned paired datasets, the proposed approach leverages an unpaired dataset of approximately 4,000 images, curated from the public ToothFairy dataset. The architecture integrates U-Net-based generators and PatchGAN discriminators, specifically tuned to mitigate generative hallucinations and preserve morphological integrity. Quantitative benchmarking on a held-out test set demonstrates a 34.6\% improvement in the Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) score, a substantial reduction in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) from 207.03 to 157.04, and a superior Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.9105. The framework achieves real-time efficiency with a 3.03 ms inference time per slice, effectively suppressing artifacts while preserving anatomical detail. Expert validation confirms high fidelity; however, to ensure reliability in extreme cases, the architecture is recommended as a clinical decision-support tool under human-in-the-loop oversight.
