By enhancing diagnostic clarity via a scalable software pipeline, this study provides a robust solution for high-fidelity dental implant imaging.

</details>


### [27] [Distribution-Alignment Bridge for Uncertainty-Aware Text-to-Video Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20984)
*Kyeongmo Chae,Jihoon Lee,Sangtae Ahn*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB) for text-to-video retrieval by modeling text and video as Gaussian embeddings and aligning distributions via a diffusion-inspired bridge; uses a KL-based distribution-aware contrastive loss; achieves state-of-the-art results on MSR-VTT, MSVD, VATEX and provides calibrated uncertainty-aware ranking.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Deterministic pointwise matching in cross-modal retrieval underestimates modality-specific uncertainty and ignores distributional structure; a probabilistic, distribution-alignment framework can better capture ambiguity and improve ranking reliability.

Method: Represent both text and video as Gaussian distributions (mean and variance). Employ a deterministic, diffusion-inspiredbridge that iteratively refines text distributions toward the target video distributions through a truncated refinement process. Train end-to-end to unify probabilistic embedding with distributional transformation. Optimize cross-modal similarity with a distribution-aware contrastive loss based on KL divergence.

Result: Extensive evaluations on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX show DAB significantly outperforms existing probabilistic and diffusion-based baselines and provides calibrated uncertainty-aware ranking via bridge-induced distributional margins.

Conclusion: DAB offers a unified probabilistic-embedding framework with a distributional transformation module, enabling calibrated, uncertainty-aware text-to-video retrieval and strong empirical performance on standard benchmarks.

Abstract: This paper proposes the Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB), a framework that reconceptualizes text-to-video retrieval as a distribution alignment task rather than traditional deterministic point matching. By modeling both text and video embeddings as Gaussian distributions defined by mean and variance, DAB explicitly accounts for modality-specific uncertainty. We employ a deterministic, diffusion-inspired bridge to iteratively refine text distributions toward their target video distributions through a truncated refinement process. This approach unifies probabilistic embedding and distributional transformation into a cohesive, end-to-end trainable system. To optimize cross-modal similarity, we introduce a distribution-aware contrastive loss based on Kullback-Leibler divergence. Extensive evaluations on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX benchmarks confirm that DAB significantly outperforms existing probabilistic and diffusion-based baselines, while providing calibrated uncertainty-aware ranking through bridge-induced distributional margins.

</details>


### [28] [HyWorldVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Hybrid World Modeling for Autonomous Driving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20988)
*Quanfu Yu,Xian Wu,Hao Xu,Liulong Ma*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A hybrid vision-language-action (VLA) model, HyWorldVLA, unifies pixel-level supervision with latent world modeling to improve robustness and interpretability in autonomous driving. It pre-trains by predicting video latents via a video VAE while reconstructing frames for pixel grounding, then fine-tunes to predict latent features fed into an action expert for trajectories, achieving state-of-the-art performance on NAVSIM v1/v2 and establishing a new benchmark for world-model noise robustness.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Pixel-level future prediction offers fine-grained spatiotemporal reasoning but is brittle in noisy driving; latent world models are robust but lack interpretability and pixel grounding. A hybrid approach aims to combine the strengths of both.

Method: Hybrid architecture that jointly uses pixel-level supervision and latent representation learning. In pre-training, the model predicts latent codes encoded by a pre-trained video VAE and reconstructs video frames for pixel grounding. In co-fine-tuning, the model predicts latent features only, which are used by an action expert to generate driving trajectories.

Result: HyWorldVLA significantly outperforms both pixel-based and latent-based world-model baselines on NAVSIM v1 and v2. The work also provides the first comprehensive qualitative and quantitative assessment of world-model noise robustness in autonomous driving and introduces a benchmark for evaluating such robustness.

Conclusion: A hybrid world-model framework effectively balances interpretability and robustness, offering improved performance and a new standard for evaluating noise robustness in autonomous driving models.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models augmented with world modeling represent a promising paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving. While pixel-level future prediction enables fine-grained spatiotemporal reasoning, it compromises robustness in noisy driving scenarios. Conversely, latent-based world models alleviate this sensitivity but often incur limited interpretability and representational degradation due to absent pixel-level grounding. To reconcile this trade-off, we propose HyWorldVLA, a hybrid world-VLA framework that unifies pixel-level supervision and latent representation learning. In the pre-training stage, HyWorldVLA predicts video latents encoded by a pre-trained video VAE, while simultaneously reconstructing video frames to provide precise pixel-level grounding. During the subsequent co-fine-tuning phase, the model exclusively predicts latent features, which are fed into an action expert to generate trajectories. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks demonstrate that HyWorldVLA significantly outperforms both pixel-based and latent-based world model baselines. Notably, we present the first comprehensive qualitative and quantitative analysis of world model noise robustness in autonomous driving, establishing a new benchmark for evaluating future architectures.

</details>


### [29] [Latent Variable-Mediated Cross-Learning for Few-Shot Acoustic Impedance Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20989)
*Junheng Peng,Yong Li,Mingwei Wang,Yi Bao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RD-SCL combines differentiable Tikhonov deconvolution with semi-supervised cross-learning to tackle ill-posed acoustic impedance imaging by jointly estimating latent wavelets and enforcing consistency between labeled and unlabeled traces, achieving state-of-the-art results with a small parameter count.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Acoustic impedance imaging is notoriously ill-posed due to an unknown seismic wavelet, observations that are band-limited, and scarce labeled well-log samples. Prior semi-supervised methods either rely on inaccurate wavelet priors or introduce extra networks that hinder stability and performance.

Method: Introduce a differentiable, closed-form first-order Tikhonov deconvolution operator that dynamically estimates the latent wavelet in the frequency domain during training. Build a symmetric cross-learning scheme to enforce consistency between predictions on labeled and unlabeled data, avoiding auxiliary networks and fixed priors.

Result: Empirical validation on SEAM and Marmousi 2 benchmarks shows RD-SCL outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised approaches, with substantial performance gains and lower computational cost. The model has only 56.5k learnable parameters and competitive runtime.

Conclusion: RD-SCL provides a physically grounded, efficient, and practical solution for acoustic impedance imaging, combining stable deconvolution-based wavelet estimation with semi-supervised cross-learning to better exploit unlabeled data.

Abstract: Acoustic impedance imaging is a fundamental yet severely ill-posed problem in subsurface analysis: the seismic wavelet is unknown, observations are band-limited, and labeled well-log samples are extremely scarce (typically <1% of all traces). Existing semi-supervised deep learning methods mitigate few-shot problem by incorporating forward modeling, yet they either rely on inaccurate prior wavelet assumptions or introduce auxiliary networks, leading to unstable optimization and degraded performance. We propose RD-SCL, a novel framework that integrates regularized deconvolution with semi-supervised cross-learning. At its core lies a differentiable, closed-form first-order Tikhonov deconvolution operator that dynamically estimates the latent wavelet in the frequency domain during training, providing stable physics-guided feedback without explicit auxiliary networks and fixed wavelet priors. Building on this operator, we design a symmetric cross-learning that enforces consistency between predictions on labeled and unlabeled data, thereby effectively exploiting abundant unlabeled traces. Extensive experiments on the SEAM and Marmousi 2 benchmarks demonstrate that RD-SCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and semi-supervised methods, achieving substantial gains with lower computational cost. With only 56.5k learnable parameters and competitive runtime, RD-SCL offers a practical, physically consistent, and efficient solution for acoustic impedance imaging.

</details>


### [30] [Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20993)
*Farhad Nooralahzadeh,Lea Bogensperger,Christian Bluethgen,Michael Krauthammer*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Sparse, training-free concept-channel probes reveal radiological findings in frozen 3D medical VLMs are encoded by a small set of ~10 vision channels; ablation selectively destabilizes the target finding while others remain; the sparse probe generalizes across architectures (Pillar-0 and Merlin). CCP with a report template outperforms CT-CHAT with much lower latency (F1 0.549 vs 0.184; BLEU 0.483 vs 0.373).


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand how clinical findings are represented in frozen medical encoders, identify the specific channels responsible, and assess cross-model generalization and potential for efficient clinical NLG.

Method: Probe frozen vision embeddings of Pillar-0 to identify sparse channel subsets (~10) per radiological finding; ablative analysis to check impact on findings; test the same sparse probe on an unrelated 3D VLM (Merlin); develop a training-free CCP using a corpus-derived report template; compare clinical efficacy and NLG metrics against CT-CHAT; measure latency.

Result: Each radiological finding is encoded by a sparse set of ~10 vision-encoder channels; disabling those channels collapses the corresponding finding score while unrelated labels remain stable; the same sparse probe replicates on Merlin, indicating generalizability; CCP with a report template achieves F1 0.549 and BLEU 0.483, at ~22x lower latency than CT-CHAT (F1 0.184, BLEU 0.373).

Conclusion: Frozen medical encoders encode findings via interpretable, sparse channel subsets; training-free CCP is effective for probing and improving clinical utility, with cross-model applicability.

Abstract: Large vision-language models are becoming increasingly dominant in 3D medical image interpretation, but we rarely know <i>which</i> internal units encode clinical findings or <i>where</i> that information lives in the representation. We first study this on a 3D chest vision-language model (Pillar-0) by probing its frozen vision embeddings. We show that (i) each radiological finding is encoded by a <i>sparse</i> set of ~10 vision-encoder channels that match full-feature classification performance and far exceed a zero-shot text prompting; (ii) turning off the channels tied to one finding, that finding's score collapses while unrelated labels stay stable; and (iii) the same sparse probe <i>replicates</i> on an architecturally unrelated 3D abdominal VLM (Merlin) suggesting a general property of frozen medical encoders. Our training-free concept channel probe (CCP) method, paired with a corpus-derived report template, outperforms published CT-CHAT on clinical efficacy and NLG metrics (F1 0.549 vs. 0.184; BLEU 0.483 vs. 0.373) at 22x lower latency. Our results provide a clear, reproducible characterization of how frozen medical encoders represent findings, demonstrating direct applicability across models.

</details>


### [31] [AUCH-Net: Action Unit-Based Consistency-Aware Hypergraph Network for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Facial Expression Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21004)
*Xinhan Qiu,Yan Yan,Rui Zhu,Si Chen,Hanzi Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes AUCH-Net, a cross-domain few-shot FER method leveraging action units (AUs) with consistency-aware hypergraphs. It introduces an AU feature learning (AFL) module and a visual feature learning (VFL) module with relation consistency and regularization/classification losses to learn transferable AU- and visual-features, achieving state-of-the-art results on in-lab and in-the-wild datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Cross-domain few-shot FER suffers from large domain shifts and scarce target samples. AUs offer semantically consistent, transferable cues across domains, enabling better alignment between fine-grained facial muscle movements and high-level expressions.

Method: AUCH-Net builds consistency-aware hypergraphs on AUs and learns AU features via AFL with relation consistency loss and AU regularization loss. The VFL module learns visual features guided by relation consistency loss and a classification loss. The model jointly exploits AU-visual relationships to improve cross-domain transferability, aligning AU interactions with expression categories.

Result: Extensive experiments on both in-the-lab and in-the-wild datasets show that AUCH-Net consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods, indicating that modeling AU relationships is beneficial for CF-FER under cross-domain few-shot settings.

Conclusion: Modeling AU relationships with consistency-aware hypergraphs and dual AFL/VFL learning yields superior transferable representations for CF-FER, demonstrating the potential of AUs as a bridging semantic layer across domains and expression categories.

Abstract: Recently, cross-domain few-shot facial expression recognition (CF-FER) has received considerable attention. However, the performance of existing CF-FER methods is still unsatisfactory due to inferior transferable feature learning under large domain discrepancy and limited target samples. Fortunately, the action units (AUs), which indicate the movements of different facial muscles, provide consistent conceptual semantics for describing expressions within and across domains. Inspired by this, we propose a novel Action Unit-based Consistency-aware Hypergraph Network (AUCH-Net), which constructs consistency-aware hypergraphs on AUs, for CF-FER. Specifically, AUCH-Net presents a new AU feature learning (AFL) module and a new visual feature learning (VFL) module. The AFL module learns AU features under the guidance of a novel relation consistency loss and an AU regularization loss, while the VFL module learns visual features supervised by a relation consistency loss and a classification loss. By learning consistent AU features, AUCH-Net effectively models the connections between AUs and expression categories. As a result, we can bridge the gap between fine-grained facial variations and high-level expression categories, greatly facilitating the learning of transferable feature representations.Extensive experiments on both in-the-lab and in-the-wild datasets show that our method consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. Our results clearly show that modeling the relationships among AUs holds significant potential for FER under cross-domain few-shot scenarios.

</details>


### [32] [TransBiolab: A Real-World Multi-View Dataset of Cluttered Transparent Biomedical Objects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21071)
*Ke Ma,Yifei Wang,Meng Wang,Tian Xia*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces TrainsBiolab, a large real-world RGB-D, multi-view dataset for cluttered transparent biomedical objects with 6D poses, masks, depth, and camera calibration across 15 object types, enabling segmentation, depth/pose benchmarks and robot manipulation evaluation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current datasets inadequately cover the combined challenges of clutter, occlusion, and calibrated multi-view capture in laboratory manipulation of transparent objects, limiting progress in perception and robotics.

Method: Collection of real-world RGB-D multi-view sequences from 98 scenes, totaling 161,315 frames and 1.03 million instance annotations across 15 object types; annotations include full/visible masks, depth, 6D poses, and per-frame camera calibration; organization along difficulty axes (object category, object count per frame, viewpoint); definition of dataset-centric benchmarks for segmentation, depth estimation/completion, and 6D pose estimation; inclusion of a system-level robot manipulation evaluation.

Result: A new resource enabling evaluation and development of segmentation, depth estimation/completion, 6D pose estimation, and multi-view reasoning in cluttered, occluded, transparent-object scenes; supports repeated-instance and multi-view laboratory manipulation research; project page provided for access and benchmarks.

Conclusion: TrainsBiolab fills a gap in real-world, multi-view, cluttered transparent-object datasets and is poised to accelerate perception and manipulation research in autonomous laboratories.

Abstract: Autonomous biomedical laboratories increasingly rely on visual perception to recognize, localize, and manipulate transparent plasticware, yet high-quality real-world datasets for this setting remain limited. The scarcity of domain-relevant data is particularly restrictive in cluttered multi-object scenes, where mutual occlusion and view-dependent appearance changes remain challenging even for contemporary visual foundation models. Existing transparent-object datasets have advanced segmentation, depth, and pose estimation, but they usually do not evaluate the combined setting of multi-object clutter, occlusion, and calibrated multi-view capture that characterizes real laboratory manipulation scenes. To address this gap, we present TrainsBiolab, a real-world RGB-D dataset of cluttered transparent biomedical objects captured as calibrated multi-view sequences. TrainsBiolab contains 161,315 frames from 98 scenes and 1.03M instance annotations over 15 laboratory object types, including 6D poses, full and visible masks, depth, and per-frame camera calibration. The dataset is organized along three axes that reflect operational difficulty: object category, the total number of objects in a frame, and camera viewpoint. We further define dataset-centric benchmarks for segmentation, depth estimation and completion, and 6D pose estimation, and report a system-level robot manipulation evaluation enabled by the released annotations and calibrations. By focusing on repeated transparent instances, clutter, and multi-view laboratory capture, TrainsBiolab provides a resource for segmentation, depth estimation, 6D pose estimation, and multi-view reasoning in autonomous laboratory manipulation. Project page: https://dualtransparency.github.io/TransBiolab/.

</details>


### [33] [Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21007)
*Abhijeet Narang,Kartik Kuckreja,Shreya Ghosh,Muhammad Haris Khan,Usman Tariq,Jianfei Cai,Abhinav Dhall*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A challenge and benchmark for explainable deepfake detection on XPlainVerse, combining image classification and grounded NL explanations; evaluation merges accuracy with semantic similarity, simplicity, and grounding to manipulated entities and evidence; code available.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To provide end-to-end explainable deepfake detection for real-world verification; diverse users require both correctness and justificatory explanations; scaling to million-scale dataset.

Method: Design of Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 built on XPlainVerse; dual explanations per image (detailed for technical users, concise for general users); evaluation combines standard classification metrics with explanation-oriented metrics (semantic similarity, simplicity, grounding).

Result: Introduction of the benchmark and evaluation protocol; baseline models and code provided; aims to foster development of next-generation explainable detectors.

Conclusion: The challenge will catalyze advancements in explainable deepfake detection by integrating classification with semantically grounded explanations and broad usability.

Abstract: Deepfake detection is moving beyond binary classification decisions toward systems that can also explain the visual evidence supporting those decisions. This transition is important for real-world verification settings, where diverse users need to understand not only whether an image is manipulated, but also why it is considered suspicious. The Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026 is designed to benchmark this joint capability. Built on XPlainVerse, a million-scale benchmark for explainable deepfake detection, the challenge evaluates methods on image classification and grounded natural-language explanation generation. Participants submit a real/fake label together with two explanations for each image: a detailed complex explanation for technical users and a concise simple explanation for general users. The evaluation combines classification metrics with semantic similarity, simplicity, and intent-aware grounding metrics that assess whether explanations identify the relevant manipulated entities and supporting visual evidence. The methodologies developed through the challenge will contribute to the development of next-generation explainable deepfake detectors. Evaluation script, baseline models, and accompanying code are available on https://github.com/Abhijeet8901/XPlainVerse-ACMChallenge.

</details>


### [34] [HGeo-TopoMap: Boosting Topological Mapping with Hierarchical Geometric Priors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21281)
*Siyu Li,Kunyu Peng,Di Wen,Beiping Hou,Zhiyong Li,Kailun Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Hierarchical topological mapping for autonomous driving using a geometry-aware, prior-map-guided framework (HGeo-TopoMap) that detects centerlines and lane topology with improved robustness on OpenLane-V2.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Centerlines lack explicit markings in real-world scenes, making topological map construction difficult. Leveraging explicit prior maps and geometric relations can boost detection, consistency, and robustness.

Method: An IPM-derived road structure map is processed by a geometric adaptive learning module that discretely encodes semantic/spatial features; a prior-mask attention mechanism focuses on informative regions. A geometric consistency learning module enforces alignment of centerline features with identical geometric orientations via a geometry-aware decoder, ensuring spatial consistency across centerline instances. The model is evaluated on OpenLane-V2 for centerline, lane segment, and robustness benchmarks.

Result: Significant improvements in topological mapping accuracy and robustness over baselines, with consistent gains under standard and challenging conditions. Source code and weights to be released.

Conclusion: The approach effectively exploits explicit priors and geometric relations to hierarchically boost topological mapping, particularly centerline detection, suggesting strong potential for reliable autonomous driving perception in real-world scenarios.

Abstract: Topological maps are key outputs of autonomous driving perception systems, delivering essential road information for path planning. They identify instances such as centerlines and traffic signs, along with their connectivity relationships. Due to the lack of explicit markings for centerlines in real-world environments, the detection of centerline instances remains a significant challenge. To tackle this problem, we propose HGeo-TopoMap, which leverages an explicit prior map and implicit spatial relations to hierarchically boost topological mapping. First, a geometric adaptive learning module is designed for the road structure map obtained via inverse perspective mapping. This module discretely encodes semantic and spatial features from the map, followed by a prior-mask attention mechanism that selectively focuses on informative regions. Then, a geometric consistency learning module is devised, which leverages the geometric properties and spatial relationships of centerlines. Built on the geometry-aware decoder, it enforces spatial consistency by aligning features of centerline instances with identical geometric orientations. The proposed method is evaluated on the OpenLane-V2 dataset across the centerline, lane segment, and robustness benchmarks. Beyond substantial improvements in topological mapping accuracy, the proposed method offers the benefit of enhanced robustness, consistently outperforming baselines under both standard and challenging conditions. The source code and model weights will be made publicly available at https://github.com/lynn-yu/HGeo-TopoMap.

</details>


### [35] [ProCap: Prominence-guided Object Rectification for Faithful and Comprehensive Video Captioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21022)
*Debjyoti Das Adhikary,Aritra Hazra,Partha Pratim Chakrabarti*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A training-free, prominence-aware, iterative post-hoc rectification framework for video captioning that ranks detected objects by saliency, persistence, and relational dynamics to iteratively refine captions without retraining, improving completeness and reducing hallucination on MSVD and MSR-VTT.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing training-free corrections apply a single fixed pass, which can omit semantically important content; retraining caption models is expensive and impractical. A model-agnostic, scalable solution is needed to reduce hallucinations and improve completeness without changing model parameters.

Method: Introduce a lightweight scoring module that ranks detected objects by spatial saliency, temporal persistence, and relational dynamics. Then employ an iterative, prompt-driven refinement loop that uses this ranking to progressively inject missing but contextually relevant objects into the caption over multiple rounds, all post-hoc and without modifying the captioning model.

Result: Evaluation on MSVD and MSR-VTT using object-grounded automatic metrics and a 110-participant human study. Qualitative comparisons against ChatGPT and Gemini show gains in completeness (up to 48%) and reductions in hallucination (up to 45%) relative to a strong pretrained baseline, without retraining or reference captions.

Conclusion: Prominence-guided iterative rectification is a lightweight, scalable, and model-agnostic approach that yields more complete and trustworthy video captions, with direct benefits for accessibility, retrieval, and multimedia understanding.

Abstract: Improving video captioning quality typically demands retraining large vision-language models, an expensive and often impractical requirement. Existing training-free alternatives instead ground captions in detected objects to curb hallucination, but apply only a single, fixed correction pass without prioritizing which objects matter most, leaving semantically significant content omitted. We propose a prominence-aware, iterative post-hoc rectification framework that overcomes both limitations without modifying the underlying captioning model's parameters: a lightweight scoring mechanism ranks detected objects by spatial saliency, temporal persistence, and relational dynamics, and an iterative, prompt-driven refinement loop uses this ranking to progressively inject missing yet contextually relevant objects into the caption over multiple rounds. We validate the framework on MSVD and MSR-VTT using object-grounded automatic metrics, a 110-participant human study, and qualitative comparison against ChatGPT and Gemini; in human evaluation, the framework raises perceived completeness by up to 48% and reduces hallucination by up to 45% relative to a strong pretrained captioning baseline, all without retraining or reference captions. These results position prominence-guided iterative rectification as a lightweight, scalable, and model-agnostic route to more complete and trustworthy video captioning, with direct relevance to accessibility, retrieval, and other multimedia understanding applications.

</details>


### [36] [WAT3R: Feedforward Underwater 3D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21023)
*Jiayi Xu,Jiahao Lu,Ziqiang Zheng,Yihao Tan,Yaolong Zhu,Yuan Liu,Sai-Kit Yeung*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: WAT3R is a feed-forward underwater 3D reconstruction framework that uses a degradation-adaptive, geometry-constrained neural module to output pixel-aligned 3D point maps and camera poses in a single forward pass, outperforming state-of-the-art on multiple underwater datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Underwater imaging suffers from severe light attenuation and backscattering, which degrade visual quality and disrupt feature consistency across views, hindering accurate multi-view geometry.

Method: A lightweight neural adaptation module is integrated into a feed-forward network to flexibly account for underwater imaging effects, treating degradation adaptation as a geometry-constrained process. The system outputs pixel-aligned 3D point maps and camera poses directly from underwater videos in one forward pass.

Result: Experiments on FLSea, SQUID, and USOD10K show that the method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on 3D reconstruction tasks, including multi-view/monocular depth estimation and camera pose estimation.

Conclusion: WAT3R provides efficient, high-quality underwater 3D reconstruction in a single forward pass by leveraging degradation-adaptive, geometry-constrained learning, enabling improved multi-view reconstruction in challenging underwater conditions.

Abstract: Reliable feedforward underwater 3D reconstruction remains challenging due to severe light attenuation and backscattering, which degrade visual quality and disrupt feature consistency across views, leading to inaccurate multi-view geometry. To address this issue, we propose WAT3R, a feed-forward framework for reconstructing 3D scenes directly from underwater images. By leveraging degradation adaptation as a geometry-constrained process, WAT3R integrates a lightweight neural adaptation module to flexibly account for these underwater imaging effects, thereby improving multi-view reconstruction quality. Implemented in a single forward pass, WAT3R directly and efficiently outputs pixel-aligned 3D point maps and camera poses from underwater videos, allowing a high-quality underwater 3D reconstruction. Experiments conducted on the FLSea, SQUID, and USOD10K datasets show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on 3D reconstruction tasks, including multi-view/monocular depth estimation and camera pose estimation.

</details>


### [37] [GroupVideo: Multi-Identity Customized Text-to-Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21027)
*Xinyang Song,Libin Wang,Jianxin Sun,Qi Li,Dandan Zheng,JingDong Chen,Zhenan Sun*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GroupVideo uses multimodal identity alignment and diffusion-based video generation to create identity-customized videos for multiple characters, supported by a 20k-video multi-ID dataset.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current single-identity video generation methods struggle in multi-identity settings due to identity confusion and copy-paste artifacts; there is a need for explicit identity separation, robust identity references, and natural motions in multi-ID video synthesis.

Method: Video Diffusion Transformer framework with visual alignment that encodes multiple face images as identity references and semantic alignment via a semantic perceiver to improve motion naturalness; an ID localization module with spatial guidance to prevent identity blending; bounding box constraints and mask regularization losses to focus learning on facial regions; a curated 20k-video multi-ID dataset.

Result: GroupVideo outperforms existing methods in generating multi-character videos with consistent identities and natural motions.

Conclusion: Demonstrates effective multi-ID video generation and provides a large-scale dataset to accelerate future research, addressing identity blending and motion naturalness in multi-ID scenarios.

Abstract: Current identity customized video generation methodologies are predominantly limited to single-identity scenarios, as the lack of explicit identity separation mechanisms often leads to identity confusion in multi-identity settings. Existing multi-identity approaches, which directly extend single-identity frameworks by concatenating face images as input conditions, frequently result in unnatural facial expressions and motions, manifesting as the "copy-paste" phenomenon. To overcome these limitations, we introduce GroupVideo, a novel framework that leverages multiple individual photographs to generate identitycustomized video. Built upon Video Diffusion Transformers, GroupVideo incorporates multimodal identity alignment: visual alignment jointly encodes multiple face images to provide robust identity references, while semantic alignment introduces a semantic perceiver to enhance the naturalness of motions. An ID localization module with spatial guidance is introduced to address identity blending and enhance identity fidelity, along with bounding box constraints and mask regularization loss, to focus on facial regions and improve training efficiency. In response to the shortage of multi-ID video datasets, we have curated a comprehensive high-quality dataset of 20,000 videos, thereby establishing a crucial resource to advance future research in multi-ID video generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GroupVideo outperforms existing methods in generating multi-character videos with consistent identities and natural motions.

</details>


### [38] [Spectral-Spatial Synergistic Guided Network for Hyperspectral Salient Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21032)
*Yanyan Peng,Tingfa Xu,Yao Xiao,Peifu Liu,Shuyan Bai,Fengxiang Xu,Jianan Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: We propose S3GNet, a lightweight hyperspectral salient object detector that uses spectral-structure-aware modeling, stream-aware attention, and progressive refinement to achieve robust, efficient detection under varying illumination.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Hyperspectral saliency is confounded by illumination-induced spectral variations that mimic material properties; a robust spectral-spatial representation is needed.

Method: Introduce S3GNet with (1) a parameter-free Spectral Structure-Aware Module using spectral derivatives and regional hierarchical modeling; (2) a Stream-Aware Attention Module enabling cross-stream global interaction and intra-stream spatial guidance; (3) a Progressive Gated Refinement Decoder for multi-scale feature fusion and precise boundary recovery; all in a lightweight, closed-loop information flow centered on structure perception.

Result: Empirical results show S3GNet achieves superior computational efficiency and detection accuracy over existing methods on benchmark datasets.

Conclusion: The proposed spectral-structure-guided framework yields robust, illumination-invariant saliency detection in hyperspectral images with efficient performance and accurate boundaries.

Abstract: Hyperspectral salient object detection aims to identify visually salient regions from hyperspectral images. Existing methods often fail because they fundamentally misunderstand the data, confusing incidental spectral variations caused by external factors such as illumination with essential spectral differences caused by the intrinsic material properties of the object. This leads to fragile representations and noisy predictions. To this end, we propose a lightweight and efficient Spectral-Spatial Synergistic Guided Network (S3GNet), with structure perception as the core, to build a closed-loop information flow around spectrum robust modeling, cross-stream co-perception and multi-scale refinement decoding. S3GNet introduces a parameter-free Spectral Structure-Aware Module that leverages spectral derivatives and regional hierarchical modeling to extract intrinsic features of robustness against illumination variations. Our Stream-Aware Attention Module achieves effective spectral-spatial collaboration through inter-stream global interaction and intra-stream spatial guidance. Furthermore, a Progressive Gated Refinement Decoder ensures precise object boundaries and detail recovery by optimally integrating multi-scale features. Experimental results show that S3GNet achieves superior performance in both computational efficiency and detection accuracy compared to existing methods.

</details>


### [39] [GeoThreat: Transferable Targeted Adversarial Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing Image Interpretation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21036)
*Yimin Fu,Yuefeng Bai,Baicheng Pan,Zhunga Liu,Michael K. Ng*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GeoThreat is a transferable targeted adversarial attack on LVLMs for remote sensing image interpretation, exploiting both conceptual and perceptual representations to manipulate outputs under black-box settings.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Remote sensing LVLMs lack robust evaluation against adversarial, cross-modal manipulation; remote sensing requires joint local and global reasoning, making targeted manipulation under black-box settings challenging and transferable.

Method: Uses surrogate image encoders to obtain conceptual class tokens and distills perceptual representations from adversarial patch tokens via collaborative importance estimation. Incorporates adversarial-target similarity gradients to assess cue relevance, performs cross-attentive alignment of perceptual with target tokens, and updates perturbations via ensemble-based joint optimization of conceptual calibration and perceptual adaptation.

Result: Extensive experiments show GeoThreat achieves superior transferability and controllability across diverse LVLMs compared to baselines.

Conclusion: GeoThreat demonstrates effective transferable targeted manipulation of LVLM outputs for remote sensing interpretation, highlighting vulnerability and informing defense; the framework combines conceptual and perceptual representations with gradient-based alignment to guide perturbation under black-box conditions.

Abstract: Adversarial attacks against large vision-language models (LVLMs) serve as an effective means of assessing their robustness in cross-modal semantic understanding. Existing studies mainly focus on corrupting visual inputs to induce predefined erroneous responses in general vision-language tasks, whereas corresponding investigations in remote sensing fields remain largely underexplored. Compared with natural image understanding, remote sensing image interpretation requires joint reasoning over local discriminative cues and global scene context. This poses additional challenges to achieving transferable semantic manipulation toward specified responses under black-box settings. To tackle these challenges, we propose GeoThreat, a transferable targeted adversarial attack method against LVLMs for remote sensing image interpretation. Specifically, GeoThreat modulates adversarial representations in accordance with the target content at both conceptual and perceptual levels. The class tokens from surrogate image encoders are employed as conceptual representations, while perceptual representations are distilled from patch tokens of the adversarial example through collaborative importance estimation. Beyond merely rolling out attention scores across layers, we incorporate adversarial-target similarity gradients to more faithfully characterize the relevance of local visual cues to the intended semantic manipulation. The perceptual representations are then dynamically aligned with target patch tokens in a cross-attentive manner, facilitating the adaptation of local cues toward designated semantic details. Finally, adversarial perturbations are iteratively updated via ensemble-based joint optimization of conceptual calibration and perceptual adaptation. Extensive experiments across diverse LVLMs demonstrate the superiority of GeoThreat in both transferability and controllability.

</details>


### [40] [HyperImageNet: A Large-Scale High-Spatial Resolution Hyperspectral Imagery Classification Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21050)
*Chuguang Zeng,Jingtao Li,Yinhe Liu,Yanfei Zhong*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: HyperImageNet is a large-scale hyperspectral dataset for fine-grained land-cover understanding, featuring 26k airborne image patches, 224 spectral bands, 138 fine-grained classes, and rich annotations (raw imagery, pixel labels, and instance masks) to support semantic and instance segmentation, plus an open-environment benchmark with strict spatial separation to evaluate methods and the HyperFree model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a need for comprehensive, richly annotated hyperspectral data and robust evaluation protocols that can support fine-grained land-cover understanding and open-environment (cross-domain or generalizable) remote sensing research. Existing datasets often lack either spectral breadth, fine-grained labels, pixel/instance annotations, or rigorous evaluation splits.

Method: Construct a large-scale airborne hyperspectral dataset with 26,084 patches, 224 spectral bands, and 138 fine-grained classes. Provide raw imagery, pixel-level semantic labels, and object-level instance masks to enable semantic and instance segmentation. Establish an open-environment benchmark with strict spatial separation to ensure fair evaluation and to assess generalization, including evaluation of the HyperFree foundation model alongside representative methods.

Result: Empirical results indicate that HyperImageNet effectively supports fine-grained hyperspectral understanding and open-environment remote sensing research. The dataset and benchmark enable semantic and instance segmentation tasks and demonstrate the practicality of evaluating methods and a strong baseline (HyperFree) in open-environment settings.

Conclusion: HyperImageNet delivers a comprehensive, richly annotated hyperspectral resource and an open-environment benchmark that advance fine-grained land-cover understanding and remote sensing research, with immediate applicability to semantic and instance segmentation tasks and evaluation of foundation-model-based approaches.

Abstract: We present HyperImageNet, a large-scale benchmark for fine-grained hyperspectral land-cover understanding. The dataset contains 26,084 airborne hyperspectral image patches with 224 spectral bands and 138 fine-grained land-cover categories. Unlike existing datasets, HyperImageNet provides raw imagery, pixel-level semantic labels, and object-level instance masks, supporting both semantic and instance segmentation. Furthermore, we establish an open-environment benchmark with strict spatial separation to evaluate representative methods and the HyperFree foundation model. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of HyperImageNet for fine-grained hyperspectral understanding and open-environment remote sensing research.

</details>


### [41] [Achieving Text-based Person Retrieval with Any Granularity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21057)
*Jialong Zuo,Hanyu Zhou,Dongyue Wu,Yongtai Deng,Mengdan Tan,Nong Sang,Changxin Gao,Xiang Bai*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces Text-based Person Retrieval with Any Granularity, including a five-level granularity spectrum, UFine6926-MG dataset, MG-Eval benchmark, and the CMAM framework that achieves state-of-the-art performance across granularities.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses the critical yet under-explored issue of query granularity uncertainty in text-based person retrieval, highlighting the need for a formal granularity spectrum, comprehensive multi-granular data, and evaluation protocols to model many-to-many matches.

Method: Formalize a five-level granularity spectrum; build UFine6926-MG annotated with a Multi-grained Text Annotation Engine; propose MG-Eval with progressively detailed texts and cross-identity labels; develop Cross-modal Multi-grained Aligning and Matching (CMAM) with (1) orthogonal-expert perception to disentangle granularity-specific features, (2) probabilistic alignment for many-to-many matches under query uncertainty, (3) granularity-consistent reasoning via joint cross-modal granularity verification; define training and evaluation protocols.

Result: CMAM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all granularity levels on the proposed benchmarks; the work provides a foundational multi-granular benchmark and robust baseline for practical text-based person retrieval.

Conclusion: Presents a foundational benchmark and a robust framework enabling practical, granularity-aware text-based person retrieval, encouraging development of systems that handle diverse query granularities.

Abstract: Text-based person retrieval faces a critical but under-explored challenge: the inherent uncertainty of query granularity in real-world scenarios. This paper introduces a new paradigm, Text-based Person Retrieval with Any Granularity, and provides a systematic solution. First, we formalize a five-level granularity spectrum and construct UFine6926-MG, a high-quality multi-grained dataset annotated comprehensively at all granularities via a novel Multi-grained Text Annotation Engine. Second, acknowledging that coarse queries naturally correspond to multiple valid candidates, we propose MG-Eval, a holistic evaluation benchmark with progressively detailed texts and cross-identity labels that reflect real-world semantics, alongside tailored evaluation metrics and protocols. Third, after a comprehensive diagnosis reveals the systemic limitations of existing research, we propose the Cross-modal Multi-grained Aligning and Matching (CMAM) framework. CMAM achieves granularity-aware retrieval through: 1) orthogonal-expert perception to disentangle granularity-specific features; 2) probabilistic alignment to model many-to-many matches under query uncertainty; and 3) granularity-consistent reasoning to steer feature learning via joint cross-modal granularity verification. Experiments demonstrate that CMAM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all granularity levels. This work establishes a foundational benchmark and a robust baseline, paving the way for more practical person retrieval systems.

</details>


### [42] [MVEI & EmObserver: Empowering MLLM-Oriented Visual Emotional Intelligence via Emotion Statement Judgement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21061)
*Daiqing Wu,Dongbao Yang,Jiashu Yao,Hongrui Zhang,Can Ma,Yu Zhou,Sicheng Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes Emotion Statement Judgement (ESJ) to adapt AICA for open-ended MLLMs; introduces INSETS-462k data and MVEI benchmark; trains EmObserver on ESJ; demonstrates improved evaluation and reasoning in visual emotion understanding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Systematic evaluation of visual emotional intelligence in Multimodal LLMs is lacking due to paradigm mismatch, limited emotion taxonomies, contextual neglect, and costly annotation; a scalable, expressive framework is needed.

Method: Introduce ESJ as a statement-verification formulation that constrains outputs to discriminative judgments while preserving input expressiveness; develop INSETS to scale ESJ to 462k samples; construct MVEI benchmark spanning sentiment polarity, emotion interpretation, scene context, and perception subjectivity; train EmObserver via a multi-stage recipe guided by ESJ.

Result: Extensive evaluation across broad MLLMs reveals nuanced insights into current artificial visual emotional intelligence; EmObserver achieves accuracy, generalization, and reasoning-faithfulness on AICA benchmarks; ESJ/INSETS/MVEI/EmObserver form a cohesive framework; code will be released.

Conclusion: ESJ is a practical formulation for MLLM-oriented visual emotion analysis; MVEI is a comprehensive benchmark; EmObserver provides a strong baseline to advance visual emotional intelligence in MLLMs; the work delivers scalable data, evaluation protocol, and an ESJ-tuned model.

Abstract: Affective Image Content Analysis (AICA) aims to recognize and understand emotions elicited by visual content, representing an indispensable step toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). However, despite the rapid progress of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), systematic evaluation of their visual emotional intelligence remains largely absent from recent model releases. We attribute this gap to a structural mismatch between conventional AICA paradigms and the open-ended, instruction-driven nature of MLLMs, where further analysis reveals four major limitations: omission of plausible responses, limited emotion taxonomies, neglect of contextual factors, and labor-intensive annotation. To overcome these barriers, we introduce Emotion Statement Judgement (ESJ), a statement-verification formulation that preserves the expressiveness of the input space while constraining outputs to discriminative judgements. We further develop INSETS, a labor-efficient pipeline that instantiates ESJ at scale by constructing INSETS-462k and supporting MVEI, a rigorously refined benchmark spanning sentiment polarity, emotion interpretation, scene context, and perception subjectivity. Beyond evaluation, we build EmObserver, an emotion-oriented MLLM optimized on ESJ through an elaborate multi-stage recipe. Extensive evaluation of broad-spectrum MLLMs on MVEI reveals fine-grained insights into current artificial visual emotional intelligence, while experiments on multiple AICA benchmarks demonstrate the accuracy, generalization, and reasoning faithfulness of EmObserver. Collectively, these results establish ESJ as a practical formulation, MVEI as a comprehensive benchmark, and EmObserver as an advanced baseline for advancing MLLM-oriented visual emotional intelligence. Code will be released at: https://github.com/wdqqdw/EmObserver.

</details>


### [43] [Do Pathology Vision-Language Models Truly See Pathology?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21065)
*Chengyang Zhang,Wenchuan Zhang,Bo Li,Xinyu Liu,Jiaming Yang,Mengran Li,Chenxun Deng,Jie Chen,Yang Zhang,Wei Ju,Yuhao Yi,Hong Bu,Jiancheng Lv*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: PathBind benchmark reveals misalignment between pathology VLMs' answer accuracy and visual-semantic binding, introducing 2,600 samples (PathBind-VQA, PathBind-PTA, PathBind-Grounding) and showing researchers' models rely on shortcuts; 18 models evaluated on VQA benchmarks and 10 on grounding.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address three overlooked issues in pathology VLM evaluation: (1) visual evidence not always needed, (2) domain training may not improve visual binding proportionally, (3) entity-level attention is diffuse; provide robust evaluation of multimodal binding.

Method: Construct PathBind with 2,600 samples across VQA, PTA (private atlas), and grounding; apply automated filtering and expert review; evaluate 18 representative VLMs on PathBind and five existing benchmarks; evaluate 10 VLMs on PathBind-Grounding and PathVG; analyze visual-semantic binding vs answer accuracy.

Result: Current pathology VLMs show a substantial gap between answer-side performance and visual-semantic binding; Gemini-3-Pro can achieve 53.5% accuracy with no visuals; Patho-R1-7B has lower multimodal gain by 5.8 points and 3.7-point lower attention IoU vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B; PathVG attention maps are highly correlated across entities; 18 models evaluated on VQA benchmarks; 10 on grounding.

Conclusion: PathBind provides a more reliable evaluation of multimodal capabilities by focusing on binding; existing models rely on shortcuts; future work should prioritize robust visual-semantic alignment and reduce textual shortcuts.

Abstract: Pathology vision-language models (VLMs) have recently progressed rapidly and are commonly evaluated by answer accuracy on pathology VQA benchmarks. However, we dig into current evaluations and identify three overlooked issues: 1) Visual evidence is not always necessary. For instance, Gemini-3-Pro achieves 53.5% average accuracy across 5 VQA benchmarks without any visual input. 2) Domain training can improve accuracy without proportional gains in visual binding. Compared with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Patho-R1-7B exhibits a 5.8-point lower multimodal gain and a 3.7-point lower attention IoU. 3) Entity-level attention is diffuse and weakly query-specific. On PathVG, attention maps remain highly correlated across different entity queries. These issues can lead to substantial misjudgments of pathology VLMs' actual multimodal capabilities. To this end, we present PathBind, a benchmark comprising 2,600 samples: PathBind-VQA with 1,500 questions across six dimensions, PathBind-PTA with 600 questions from a private pathology teaching atlas, and PathBind-Grounding with 500 expert-curated region-level samples. Each component undergoes task-specific automated filtering and expert review to reduce textual shortcuts and improve entity-region correspondence. We evaluate 18 representative VLMs on VQA samples of PathBind and five existing pathology VQA benchmarks, and further evaluate 10 VLMs on PathBind-Grounding and PathVG. Results show that current pathology VLMs still exhibit a substantial gap between answer-side performance and visual-semantic binding.

</details>


### [44] [Show, Don't Tell: Evaluating Spatial Cognition in Generative Pixels Rather Than LLM Text](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21072)
*Xu Wang,Kaixiang Yao,Miao Pan,Xiaohe Zhou,Xuanyu Liu,Wenqi Zhang,Xuhong Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces ProVisE, a protocolized, benchmark-agnostic framework for eliciting pixel-space visual answers from image-generation models to enable metric-compatible evaluation of spatial reasoning; adds SpatialGen-Bench with 470 samples across 14 subtasks; shows complementary strengths of image-generation and text-output VLMs; validates Agentic protocol construction on external benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the mismatch between spatial reasoning benchmarks (which often require coordinates, options, or text) and image-generation models that output pixel-level content; enable fair, cross-model evaluation of spatial cognition across modalities by using pixel-space answers aligned to existing metrics.

Method: ProVisE framework that protocolizes visual answers from image-generation models and parses them into structured predictions; Agentic builder to construct/validate task-specific protocols; SpatialGen-Bench, a curated diagnostic set of 470 samples across 14 spatial subtasks, 4 capability levels, and diverse answer forms; unified evaluation of representative text-output VLMs and image-generation models; validation of Agentic protocol construction on six external spatial benchmarks.

Result: Image-generation models are competitive when spatial answers are externalized in pixel space; text-output VLMs retain an advantage in compositional spatial reasoning; indicates complementary strengths between pixel-space expression and text-based reasoning; establishes a metric-compatible testbed for studying spatial cognition in image-generation models.

Conclusion: ProVisE and SpatialGen-Bench provide a unified, protocol-driven evaluation framework that enables cross-benchmark comparisons of spatial reasoning across image-generation and text-output models, clarifying strengths and limitations and enabling systematic study of spatial cognition in multi-modal AI.

Abstract: Spatial intelligence is essential for agents to move from static semantic understanding toward interacting with the physical world. Many spatial tasks are grounded in continuous visual scenes, where locations, regions, and paths are more naturally expressed by pointing, marking, or drawing than by reporting precise coordinates or discrete textual symbols. Yet existing spatial reasoning benchmarks usually require coordinates, options, or text, creating an answer-interface mismatch for image-generation models. This makes it difficult to evaluate image-generation models under the same task semantics as text-output VLMs, despite their ability to externalize spatial judgments directly in pixel space. We propose ProVisE (Protocolized Visual Evaluation), a benchmark-agnostic framework that elicits protocol-constrained visual answers from image-generation models and parses them into structured predictions compatible with original metrics. ProVisE also includes an Agentic builder that constructs and validates task-specific protocols for new benchmarks. We further introduce SpatialGen-Bench, a curated diagnostic benchmark of 470 samples across 14 spatial subtasks, four capability levels, and diverse answer forms. We evaluate representative text-output VLMs and image-generation models in a unified setting and validate Agentic protocol construction on six external spatial benchmarks. Results show that image-generation models are competitive when spatial answers can be externalized directly in pixel space, while text-output VLMs retain a clear advantage in compositional spatial reasoning. These findings reveal complementary strengths of pixel-space expression and text-based reasoning and establish a metric-compatible testbed for studying spatial cognition in image-generation models.

</details>


### [45] [C-PTQ: Fisher-weighted Channel-wise Sensitivity for Post-training Quantization of MLLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21076)
*Jiameng Li,Han Zhou,Matthew B. Blaschko*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: C-PTQ is a Fisher-weighted, channel-wise post-training quantization (PTQ) method that aligns quantization errors with task-specific loss to protect outlier channels in LLMs, achieving state-of-the-art results without auxiliary modules.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Quantized LLMs suffer performance drops due to highly sensitive outlier channels. Existing PTQ methods rely on modality- or token-level metrics that poorly reflect channel-wise impact on the task loss, leading to suboptimal scaling.

Method: Introduce a unified channel-wise PTQ (C-PTQ) using a Fisher-weighted objective as a tractable Hessian approximation to inject task sensitivity into the channel scaling process. This aligns quantization error with the second-order loss perturbation without extra modules (no LoRA). Applicable to weight-only and weight-activation settings.

Result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Qwen2.5VL, InternVL2, and LLaVA-OV across 8 benchmarks, under both weight-only and weight-activation quantization.

Conclusion: A unified, efficient PTQ approach that improves LLM quantization by coupling channel-wise scaling with task-specific loss perturbation, enabling strong performance without additional modules.

Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require huge memory and computational costs, which limits their practical deployment. Post-training quantization (PTQ) techniques offer an efficient solution for model compression and inference acceleration. Yet, the quantized model faces performance degradation due to outlier channels, which are highly sensitive to quantization and substantially impair activation fidelity and task accuracy. To protect these salient channels during quantization, existing PTQ methods leverage modality- or token-level metrics to guide channel-wise scaling (CWS) of LLM decoders. However, these orthogonal measurements fail to capture channel-wise impacts on task-specific loss, and the misalignment between importance and scaling factors ultimately leads to suboptimal performance. To address this issue, we propose C-PTQ, a unified channel-wise PTQ method that harmonizes task-specific loss perturbation and quantization error. Motivated by second-order derivatives, we design a Fisher-weighted objective as a tractable Hessian approximation, seamlessly injecting task sensitivity into the scaling process. Notably, we achieve state-of-the-art performance without auxiliary modules like LoRA, thereby maintaining high efficiency. Experiments on Qwen2.5VL, InternVL2 and LLaVA-OV across 8 benchmarks demonstrate our effectiveness in both weight-only and weight-activation settings.

</details>


### [46] [The RealDefocus Benchmark for Defocus Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21078)
*Tim Seizinger,Zhuyun Zhou,Radu Timofte*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces RealDefocus-Benchmark for SIDD: a realistic, high-res paired defocused/sharp dataset with train/val/test splits and unified eval framework, enabling cross-dataset validation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address scarcity of realistic, aligned defocus/sharp data and lack of standardized evaluation in SIDD.

Method: Builds on RealDefocus (from RealBokeh) to provide paired inputs and ground truth, predefined splits, and a unified evaluation framework; outlines cross-dataset benchmarking protocol.

Result: Provides a reproducible benchmark and evaluation protocol for defocus deblurring, enabling robust performance assessment and generalization via cross-dataset validation.

Conclusion: Project page available at www.github.com/TimSeizinger/RealDefocus-Benchmark.

Abstract: Single-Image Defocus Deblurring (SIDD) aims to recover an all-in-focus image from a single defocused observation, but rigorous and reproducible evaluation remains challenging due to the scarcity of realistic, high-resolution datasets with well-aligned defocused/sharp pairs and standardized protocols. We build on RealDefocus, a benchmark derived from the real-world RealBokeh dataset originally proposed for Bokeh Rendering. RealDefocus provides paired defocused inputs and sharp ground truth images, predefined training/validation/test splits, and a unified evaluation framework for comparing image restoration and neural rendering approaches. We further outline a benchmarking protocol with cross-dataset validation to assess reconstruction quality and generalization. The project page is publicly available at: www.github.com/TimSeizinger/RealDefocus-Benchmark.

</details>


### [47] [Geo3R: Mitigating Spatial Reasoning Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21085)
*Mingyu Wang,Weilin Jin,Wenbo Li,Haoyang Huang,Tong Jia,Ying Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Geo3R is a training-free plug-and-play framework that mitigates spatial reasoning hallucinations in Multimodal LLMs by integrating geometric evidence and structured 3D reasoning. It identifies spatial reasoning hallucination as a subcategory of relation hallucination, and evaluates on three benchmarks covering perspective effects, object orientation, and viewpoint changes, showing substantial, model-agnostic improvements across 18 tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a persistent gap between 2D visual representations and true 3D spatial structure in MLLMs, causing hallucinations in spatial reasoning despite existing mitigation methods. This work defines spatial reasoning hallucination as a distinct problem and seeks geometry-grounded solutions.

Method: A training-free, plug-and-play framework (Geo3R) that injects geometric evidence and structured 3D reasoning into MLLMs to reduce spatial reasoning hallucination without additional model training.

Result: Empirical evaluation across three benchmarks with 18 tasks shows substantial reductions in spatial reasoning hallucinations for diverse MLLMs, outperforming existing models and mitigation methods without requiring training.

Conclusion: Geo3R demonstrates that geometry-guided, training-free mitigation can effectively address spatial reasoning hallucinations in MLLMs, with broad applicability across tasks and models; future work could explore more explicit 3D scene understanding and robustness to real-world variations.

Abstract: Despite remarkable progress in visual understanding, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) remain prone to hallucinations when reasoning about spatial relationships, often producing judgments that contradict the true 3D structure of the scene. Though several existing works have proposed to mitigate hallucinations, our analysis indicates that they show limited effectiveness in spatial reasoning, as they fail to bridge the fundamental gap between 2D visual representations and 3D spatial reality. Based on this finding, we define hallucinations arising from insufficient spatial structure modeling as spatial reasoning hallucination, a subcategory of relation hallucination that existing mitigation methods fail to address. We further identify three typical scenarios where such hallucinations frequently occur: perspective effects, object orientation, and viewpoint changes. To this end, we propose Geo3R, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that incorporates geometric evidence and structured 3D reasoning to mitigate spatial reasoning hallucination. Experiments on three benchmarks, covering 18 tasks across all three scenarios, show that Geo3R substantially reduces spatial reasoning hallucination across diverse MLLMs without additional training, outperforming existing models and methods.

</details>


### [48] [Loss Landscape Topology Reveals Why Simple Baselines are Competitive at 3D Point Cloud Segmentation Under Class Imbalance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21089)
*Antonis Savva,Christos Kyrkou,Theocharis Theocharides*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Cross-entropy with uniform weighting is a robust baseline for imbalanced 3D point cloud segmentation; specialized 2D imbalance methods offer only modest gains and can degrade if mis-tuned. The extreme imbalance creates narrow, difficult basins; moderate imbalance leads to flat plateaus, explaining limited transferability of loss-based methods from 2D to 3D, validated across two architectures.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To investigate whether imbalance-aware techniques from 2D CV translate to 3D point clouds and to understand why they may underperform. The study systematically evaluates multiple imbalance mitigation methods on 3D datasets with severe and moderate class imbalance.

Method: Systematic evaluation of 11 imbalance mitigation approaches across datasets with extreme (641:1) and moderate (56:1) class imbalance. Analyzes error patterns, decision boundaries, and optimization landscape geometry (topology of loss landscapes). Validation across two representative point-based architectures.

Result: Standard cross-entropy with uniform weighting achieves competitive performance, typically within 0.8-3.3% mIoU of specialized methods, regardless of architecture/dataset. Imbalance severity shapes the loss landscape: extreme imbalance forms narrow basins, moderate imbalance forms flat plateaus, limiting gains from loss-level modifications. Specialized methods provide modest improvements with tight tuning; risk substantial degradation if poorly tuned.

Conclusion: Provides a mechanistic explanation for the limited transfer of 2D imbalance techniques to 3D point cloud segmentation. Recommends sticking to strong baselines (cross-entropy) for robustness, with only small, architecture/dataset-dependent gains from specialized methods. Offers guidance for practitioners and motivates further study into geometry-aware training strategies.

Abstract: Semantic segmentation of 3D point clouds faces severe class imbalance, yet the effectiveness of specialized imbalance-aware methods from 2D computer vision remains unclear in 3D contexts. We systematically evaluate 11 imbalance mitigation approaches across datasets with extreme (641:1) and moderate (56:1) imbalance ratios, revealing a surprising finding: standard cross-entropy with uniform weighting achieves competitive performance, typically within 0.8-3.3% mIoU of specialized methods across architectures and datasets. Through multifaceted mechanistic analysis of error patterns, decision boundaries, and the geometry of the optimization landscape, our analyses suggest that imbalance severity shapes the topology, creating narrow solution basins under extreme imbalance and flat plateaus under moderate imbalance. This appears to constrain the effectiveness of loss-level modifications, as all methods must navigate these geometric constraints. Our findings offer practical guidance; standard cross-entropy provides a robust baseline, with specialized methods offering modest improvements (0.8-3.3% mIoU) that vary by architecture and dataset but risk substantial degradation if poorly tuned. This work provides the first mechanistic explanation for why techniques proven effective in 2D do not readily transfer to point-based 3D point cloud segmentation, validated across two representative architectures.

</details>


### [49] [HalluScope: Fine-grained Hallucination Diagnosis for Multimodal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21105)
*Weilin Jin,Mingyu Wang,Wenbo Li,Haoyang Huang,Yifan Wu,Ying Li,Gang Huang,Zhonghai Wu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Proposes fine-grained hallucination diagnosis for multimodal LLMs, with a new HalluScope-30K dataset and two models, achieving state-of-the-art results and effective diagnosis-driven mitigation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current MLLM hallucination research relies on coarse detection, lacking diagnostic granularity to understand types and support mitigation.

Method: Automated data generation; dataset HalluScope-30K covering eight sources and five task categories; multi-granular joint reward; train HalluScope-4B and HalluScope-8B; joint optimization; interpretable explanations; evaluation on MHALO and fine-grained classification benchmarks; diagnosis-driven feedback.

Result: State-of-the-art on MHALO and their fine-grained benchmark; mutual benefits between detection and classification under joint optimization; explanations guide target models to mitigate hallucinations; full diagnosis outperforms baselines on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and LLaVA-1.5-7B.

Conclusion: Fine-grained diagnostic framework enhances understanding and mitigation of MLLM hallucinations; joint optimization improves performance and interpretable explanations can effectively guide downstream model corrections.

Abstract: Although Multimodal Large Language Models have achieved strong performance across a wide range of vision-language tasks, they still suffer from hallucinations, where model outputs become inconsistent with the visual content, textual context, or commonsense knowledge. Existing studies primarily address this problem through coarse-grained detection. However, these approaches often provide insufficient diagnostic information for understanding hallucination types and supporting downstream hallucination mitigation. To bridge this gap, we propose fine-grained hallucination diagnosis for MLLMs, a new unified task that jointly performs hallucination detection, classification, and interpretable explanation generation. We develop an automated data generation pipeline and construct HalluScope-30K, a large-scale diagnostic dataset covering eight sources and five task categories. Based on this dataset, we design a multi-granular joint reward function and train two diagnosis models, HalluScope-4B and HalluScope-8B, which achieve state-of-the-art performance on both the MHALO benchmark and our fine-grained hallucination classification benchmark. Notably, detection and classification are mutually beneficial under joint optimization. Furthermore, diagnosis-driven feedback experiments show that the fine-grained diagnostic explanations produced by our model effectively guide target models to correct their hallucinations, with full diagnosis substantially outperforming all baselines on both Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and LLaVA-1.5-7B.

</details>


### [50] [The Second LoViF 2026 Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration: Methods and Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21118)
*Xiang Chen,Hao Li,Jiangxin Dong,Jinshan Pan,Xin Li,Hongbo Ding,Junpeng Jiang,Xingyu Qiu,Yilian Zhong,Yuxiang Chen,Shibo Yin,Zixuan Huang,Yushun Fang,Xilei Zhu,Yahui Wang,Chen Lu,Xiaodong Zhou,Qingyue Cao,Changwei Gong,Jingyun Liu,Xingchen Yi,Hansen Shi,Ruiyi Liu,Jirui Xie,Tao Liu,Wenzhuo Ma,Hongzhen Li,Yongyong Chen,Zheng Zhou,Jingyong Su,Jie Liu,Haijin Zeng,Cheng Li,Peishuai Zha,Ziyi Wang,Jian Tang,Yan Chen,Long Bao,Heng Sun,Jiyuan Zhang,Shuai Liu,Wei Ding,Chengjun Guo,Yibin Huang,Xiaotao Wang,Dongqing Zou,Lei Lei,Xiaofeng Wang,Xiao Liu,Yulin Wu,Yuhan Zhao,Shurui Peng,Chao Ren,Yu-Kai Wang,Kosuke Shigematsu,Asuka Shin,Rong-Lin Jian,Cheng-Jun Kang,Jin-Hui Jiang,Jialin Zhou,Kuo Yuan,Songyu Zhang,E B Benson,Ashfaq Hussain,Pruthvikanth AC,Qirui Chen,Jinyuan Chen,Jun Zhang,Xu Zhang,Xuhui Cao,Jiaqi Ma,Laibin Chang,Yuchun Miao,Yichu Xu,Yuanzhi Yao,Shi Chen,Yuning Cui,Huan Zhang,Lefei Zhang,Saeed Ahmad,Ik Hyun Lee,Jun Young Park,Ji Hwan Yoon,Shangquan Sun,Behrooz Nobahar-Moghanlou,Majid Edalatjou,Karim Shahi-Niyar,Ruibo Zhang,Dexiang Hong,Xinyan Liu,Shengeng Tang,Weidong Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A comprehensive review of the second LoViF Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration, evaluating unified restoration across blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow; analyzes 20 finalist teams from 158 participants and provides updated benchmark and design insights.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To advance unified image restoration under diverse real-world degradations and enable robust generalization within a single framework.

Method: Collected and reproduced submitted results from 20 finalist teams; performed comprehensive analysis of submitted solutions, summarizing methods and empirical findings; extracted design strategies and benchmarked performance across degradation types.

Result: Identified effective design strategies, showcased progress in real-world all-in-one restoration, and established an updated benchmark for future research.

Conclusion: The report synthesizes advances, informs future method development, and sets a refreshed evaluation framework to drive robustness and generalization in all-in-one restoration.

Abstract: This paper presents a review of the second LoViF Challenge on Real-World All-in-One Image Restoration. The challenge aims to advance unified image restoration under diverse real-world degradation conditions, including blur, low-light, haze, rain, and snow. It provides a common benchmark for evaluating the restoration accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability of models across multiple degradation categories within a unified framework. The competition attracted 158 registered participants, and 20 teams were included in the final ranking after their submitted results were successfully reproduced and verified. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the submitted solutions and corresponding results, highlighting recent advances in real-world all-in-one image restoration. The summarized methods and empirical findings reveal effective design strategies and establish an updated benchmark for future research in real-world low-level vision.

</details>


### [51] [Causal-AgentIR: Self-Evolving Causal Memory for Adaptive Image Restoration Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21125)
*Hu Gao,Yulong Chen,Lizhuang Ma*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A hierarchical multi-agent image restoration framework with self-evolving causal memory (Causal-AgentIR) that uses a structured causal memory graph to store and reason about degradation patterns, tools, actions, quality changes, and user preferences, enabling graph-based retrieval and multi-hop causal reasoning across collaborative agents.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current restoration agents rely on static, unstructured knowledge representations, hindering long-term accumulation, verification, revision, and forgetting of restoration knowledge.

Method: Introduce Causal-AgentIR: a multi-agent system with planning, degradation analysis, tool expertise, causal memory reasoning, outcome critique, and memory curation. Represent experience as a structured causal memory graph linking degradation patterns, regions, tools, actions, quality changes, and user preferences; enable graph-based retrieval and multi-hop reasoning; implement memory operations (add/update/merge/reinforce/ignore/discard) based on quality feedback.

Result: Extensive experiments validate effectiveness, showing improved knowledge management, transferability, and restoration performance under diverse degradations.

Conclusion: A structured, causal memory-based multi-agent framework enhances long-term learning and collaboration for image restoration tasks by enabling durable knowledge, reliable reasoning, and scalable memory stewardship.

Abstract: Image restoration agents have recently emerged as a flexible paradigm for handling diverse and unpredictable degradations in real-world scenarios. Existing agents typically formulate restoration as a tool-using process, where the agent perceives degradations, searches candidate tools, executes restoration operations, and revises the plan through reflection or rollback. However, their knowledge is often stored as static tool descriptions, manually defined degradation priors, or unstructured textual summaries, which limits the accumulation, verification, revision, and forgetting of restoration knowledge over long-term experience. In this paper, we propose Causal-AgentIR, a hierarchical multi-agent framework with self-evolving causal memory for collective image restoration intelligence. Instead of representing restoration experience as isolated textual records, Causal-AgentIR organizes degradation patterns, image regions, restoration tools, actions, quality changes, and user preferences into a structured causal memory graph. This graph supports graph-based retrieval and multi-hop causal reasoning, enabling agents to infer how specific restoration operations or tool sequences affect restoration quality under different degradation conditions. The framework further organizes multiple agents into a collaborative system, including planning, degradation analysis, tool expertise, causal memory reasoning, outcome critique, and memory curation. Through this design, restoration experience can be added, updated, merged, reinforced, ignored, or discarded according to observed quality changes and feedback, allowing the agent to maintain reliable and transferable restoration knowledge.
  Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

</details>


### [52] [Safety-oriented sidewalk and road segmentation for smartphone-based assistive navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21137)
*Hakan Calim,Anamaria Dumitrescu,Adarsh Bhandary Panambur,Huzaifa Asif,Andreas Maier*

Main category: cs.CV
